But Ayame knew that tone. At least, when used on her in the bedroom, it could only mean one thing...
Her eyes went wide. "Wait-"
He buried himself to the root, launching Ayame clean off the floorboards, and held.
The venom met the deepest part of her and detonated.
"HYAAAHN❤️❤️!!"

Her legs shot out rigid on either side of him, trembling violently, toes curling hard enough to shake on their own. The orgasm that ripped through her bore no resemblance to the ones before it. This one started from her beyond-drenched folds and tore through everything the venom owned, and her whole body seized in his arms, back bowing against his chest, heels kicking at nothing.
"I... it won't... STOP... AaAHN!!"

Her release hit the sacred floorboards of the Fujimori dawn dojo from above, a brutal soaking flood that drenched his thighs, splattered the heritage wood, and pooled across the grain in a dark tide the school's founding precepts had no protocol for.
Black Fang rose and retreated two steps ahead of the advancing front.
"Quin... Quin... QUIIIN❤️❤️❤️!!"

Her body clenched and released around him in long helpless waves, each one wringing another wet rush out of her that rained down onto the boards below. Her legs jerked and trembled in the air with every spasm, until the flood had claimed everything within reach and a few things that had believed themselves safely at a distance.

When the cascading orgasm finally ended, a very long time later, her legs dropped limp against his, her body went boneless in his arms, and the last aftershock rolled through her like a shudder through a shipwreck.
"You... bastard... I'll... kill... you!"
Came the cute whimpers, making Quinlan's heart sing with joy.
Taking care of this amazing girl's unique needs was always a hard task, but he was happy to do his best.

Quinlan laid her down on the dry side of the floor with absurd gentleness, the kind of care you'd give something precious and breakable. He brushed the matted hair from her face and tucked a strand behind her ear, then pulled a discarded fold of ritual silk over her and smoothed it at the corners as if the blanket's alignment was a matter of genuine importance.
"This was..." Ayame breathed into the floor, eyes closed, "the best duel ever... Better than I ever... Could've imagined..."
She went silent, and quiet took the hall, all at once.
Quinlan straightened his spine, hands on his hips, and exhaled.
"Haaah... Another job well done."
He looked utterly smug with himself.
Then his eyes met the other conscious person's.
Snow fell past the doors.
The brazier worked through its coals.
"It was great to see this side of you. I had a lot of fun," Quinlan smiled.
"There is no side." Black Fang's voice came flat and immediate. "I helped correct a brat. I've done so many times already with Vex."
Quinlan took a step toward her.
"You corrected Vex's behavior over the years no doubt, but not like you did today."
"Today was no different."

Quinlan was still naked, still marked with everything the night had put on him, Ayame's thunderous releases visible on his thighs and the firelight making thorough use of every line of muscle it found.
He wore none of it with shame and all of it with sheer confidence.
"Come on, now." The grin widened. "Don't go crawling back into your shell. You're finally showing what's underneath it. It's wonderful."
Black Fang watched him come.
She watched the way her little sister's cocky, insufferable, shamelessly naked lover closed distance on her, unhurried and certain, and she did not like it one bit.
Her head tilted. A predator's motion, the one that preceded a kill, and she took a step of her own.
Their eyes stayed locked, two territorial psychopaths who refused to be taken out of their element.
Two steps apart, then one.
Her hand came up and landed flat on his chest, fingers spread, and held him there.
Cold.
"You are far too comfortable around me."
Quinlan's eyes lit up. He opened his mouth to answer.
"Don't get the wrong idea." Her palm pressed harder, silencing him. "Everything that happened in that cell, I did for myself."
She pushed him back half a step with a confidence that matched his own.
"You were a cow with life-saving milk, and my life was in danger, so I milked you. That is the entirety of what occurred."
Quinlan's grin began its slow, terrible climb from the corner of his mouth toward his ear.
"And what you whispered into my ear? How do you explain that, Miss Terror?"
"It expedited the extraction," Black Fang replied without a fraction of a heartbeat's delay. "A strategic move. Nothing more."

The grin reached both ears. Two unhinged predators stood a hand-span apart in the wreckage of a dawn dojo, one of them dripping with evidence and grinning like the devil himself, the other flat-eyed and immovable, and neither of them blinked.
Quinlan then took the last step, pushing through her hand until her palm bent against his chest and his fingers found her chin and tilted it up.
"I don't believe you."
He turned her head to the side in his palm while her eyes remained closely locked onto his.
"You're a liar, Black Fang~"
The temperature fell out of the room.
Black Fang's aura hit the hall like a door slamming, pure dread and menace flooding the air between them.
The brazier's flames leaned sideways and dimmed. Her bent arm straightened against his chest, her palm locking flat, and the violet in her eyes went thin and bright as venom in a needle.
Teeth bared in the same space, neither yielding a fraction, the air between them so charged it hummed.
"Say that again."
Quinlan's grin didn't waver. "Sure."
If anything, it sharpened.
"You are a liar, Black Fang."
The snow stopped falling past the veranda. The coals in the brazier went dark.

chapters.title: Chapter 1854 A Bad Liar
paragraphs: "You are a liar, Black Fang."
Black Fang did not move, and neither did the man holding her chin.
Snow had quit the garden and the coals had quit the brazier, so the only light left in the dawn dojo came off the moonlit drifts outside and the thin violet burning in her eyes.
His fingers stayed where they were, her palm stayed flat against his chest, and the cold went on pouring off her into a hall that had already given up everything it had to give.
The accusation stood between them, spoken twice and not once denied.
"I am done waiting," Black Fang decreed suddenly. "We settle everything once and for all."
"Everything...?" Quinlan's eyes began to blaze, like banked coals given air. Did 'everything' include that bet of theirs?
"Yes," she replied, eyes locked onto his. "Everything."
"Where's the rush?" His thumb stroked her chin. "A few more weeks and you win by default. You've been patient for centuries. A month is nothing."
"A month is not nothing."
Her free hand rose, and two fingers touched her own cheek, absently, checking.

"My pill will expire within hours, and I'll begin aging again. You say I was patient for centuries but..." Her fingers had drifted back to her cheek, to the same spot she had checked before. "That was only because I had no other choice."
Her chin lifted a degree inside his grip. "I do not intend to let my body begin aging again while you flounder through a courtship you can never land."

Quinlan stood there in the cold and listened to the most dangerous woman on the continent explain, with citations, why a seduction wager needed to be settled tonight for reasons of pure accounting, namely the possibility of wrinkly skin, and his face began to swim with amusement.
'Women,' he thought, from the very bottom of his soul, 'are truly amazing creatures.'
"Stop looking at me like that."
"Like what?"

Her hand left his chest, rose, and took his chin in her fingers, his own grip reflected back at him, and the two of them stood locked in the dark hall, each holding the other's face, neither owning a single step of retreat.
"Like that."
The teasing drained out of him. What stayed behind was older and stiller, and it looked at her without one gram of play.
"I would've won the bet, just to be clear. But so be it. How do you propose we settle it?"
Black Fang looked away.
Half a heartbeat. The violet slid off toward the snow garden and hauled itself back by force of will.
Quinlan's mouth opened by degrees.
"Wait." His voice dropped low. "Don't tell me. You want to..."

"I am stronger." The scoff arrived on schedule, flat as a filing. "I gave my word I would not attack you to extract your seed. Goading your bottomless hubris into open combat would be an attack wearing a disguise. That type of... duel is not an attack, and I get to stop decaying while you waste my time." Her head tilted dangerously. "It is the only structure that makes sense."
"A duel."
"Stop repeating my words back to me, I'm not mentally disabled," hissed Black Fang, suddenly looking far too adorable in Quinlan's eyes.
His joy climbed to elevations previously unrecorded.
"By the way, I couldn't help but notice." His eyes twinkled. "You really are sure that you're still stronger?"
"I am."
Zero hesitation. Not a blink of it, not a breath. And deep in Quinlan's chest, the primordial competitor came up off its throne with murder in its heart.
Then he sat it back down.
'Not tonight,' he informed it. 'Priorities.'
"Stop looking at me like that," Black Fang said again.
"I'm not looking like anything."
He released her chin. She released his one finger at a time.
And then, because he was who he was, a proper gentleman, Quinlan stepped back into the open floor, raised one hand, and called water.
It answered out of the night air, a ribbon first, then a sheet, warmed as it gathered, curling around his arms and down his chest and sluicing the long night warfare off his skin in lazy spirals.
A second finger flicked sideways, and a thread of flame crossed the hall into the dead brazier, where the coals caught, thought about it, and crawled back to red, burning only because she allowed it.
It was important to set the right atmosphere.

He washed unhurried and shameless, attending to himself as if in a private bath instead of a wrecked dojo, fully aware of the starving violet eyes tracking every pass of the water, and charging no admission.
Black Fang watched the whole performance, and her eyes were narrowing.
He washed at his own tempo, prepared at his own tempo, rolled his shoulders at his own tempo.
She had watched him do exactly this all night, to her sister, one comfortable degree at a time, until the entire battlefield ran on his clock.
Her eyes finished narrowing.
She crossed the floor without sound and shoved him.

Flat palm, center mass, measured to the ounce. The water lost its shape and rained across the boards as Quinlan went down easy, rolling through the fall like a man settling into bed, and by the time his back met the floor she was already astride him, one knee planted on either side of his hips. The bathing session was concluded, by executive order.
He looked up at her with zero shock and a rising quantity of everything else.
"What are you doing?"
"I am going on the attack," said Black Fang. "Naturally."
Madness had begun to swirl in the violet, slow and shining, the dangerous kind, the kind men with a certain taste like Quinlan wrote love letters about, and it looked obscenely good on her.
"Solid strategy," Quinlan allowed. "Aggressive, as is right. The Villain's Fang cannot be an indecisive woman."
"Shut your mouth."
"You could let me finish washing. I was doing it for you."

"For what reason?" Her hands went to the sash of her under-robe and began, without hurry, to work it loose. "My sister's fluids are already on me. Your sweat does not bother me." The knot gave, and the silk loosened off one pale shoulder. "And why would I wait, and let you set the pace?"

She undressed while mounted on him, spine straight in the firelight. The buckles came next, then the bindings, each piece drawn off and laid within reach in the order she would want them back in an emergency.

From the seams and hems, needle-fine pins slid free one by one and joined the pile in a neat row, emergency tools she had carried everywhere since the cell. The wrappings unwound from her forearms. The last pin came out of her hair, and the hair came down after it, black spilling loose past her shoulders.
Quinlan, flat on his back beneath all of this, raised one finger.
A thread of wind slipped across the dojo, collected a cushion from beside the ruined seating, and delivered it under his head, angled for a long show.
He settled in, folded his hands on his stomach, and watched his own ambush unfold with the composure of royalty at the theater.
Then, because watching was good but participating was better, he reached up to help with the tie of her last binding.
Both wrists were caught and put back down, pressed once against the boards with a pressure that closed the discussion, and released.
Her eyes stayed on his through all of it, territorial down to the last candle of violet in them.

chapters.title: Chapter 1855 At Long Last
paragraphs: '...Huh,' thought Quinlan, leaving his hands exactly where they had been filed.

She truly believed it mattered. That was the shape arriving to him while she stripped herself above him with border-guard discipline. The pace was not a preference to her, not a style. Somewhere in that beautiful, lethal head of hers, it was the entire war. If she surrendered one piece of it, one sleeve, one knot, one decision, she would not be the Venomborne Terror.
'So I can't even help her undress, huh,' he mused.
His hands found her thighs instead.
Softly. Just resting there, thumbs drawing two idle arcs along the muscle and the gorgeous purple tattoos, a presence rather than a grip. Her gaze dropped to them and her eyes narrowed.
"Surely this much is legal." He smiled up at her. "I'm letting you prepare everything you need. You do realize I could be on the attack right now, don't you?"

The narrow eyes narrowed further, and then further than that, because against her tailbone, warm and patient and unmoved by any ruling she had issued tonight, rested the full hard length of him, throbbing on its own unbothered schedule.
She elected not to dignify it.
The last silk came off her shoulders, and the firelight slid over what four hundred years had refused to touch.

Pale skin without a single scar's error. The serpent tattoos winding up both arms, still for the moment. A body built and kept like the weapon it was, and low on her belly, small and crimson, the mark that had made her his family without ever once making her his.
Quinlan drank her in, slow and thorough, top to bottom, and the want that rose up in him had months of patience behind it and nowhere left to wait.
And below the mark, where she knelt open above him, the firelight found what she had not audited: her most sacred part... Was not dry.
It wasn't an Ayame-style overflooded flower garden for sure, but neither would it be correct to call it a barren wasteland.
Quinlan had eyes. He used them.
And then he said nothing at all. No widening of the grin, no commentary, not one syllable of the teasing that lesser evidence earned by the bucket.
It gleamed there, admissible and damning, and the most shameless man alive granted the witness full immunity, because a real man does not embarrass the woman he loves on her first night.
'I'll just have to make her see reality herself,' he thought, comfortable on his pillow, and kept his counsel.
One preparation remained.
Black Fang took up the discarded under-robe, found its hem, and tore.
*Rrrip.*
A single strip of black silk came away along the grain, clean as a field dressing. She set it between her teeth.
Then, with her eyes locked on the man beneath her, both arms rose, and she gathered the loose spill of her hair off her shoulders in long handfuls and swept it high.

The pose gave him everything: her bare armpits, chest lifted, bared throat catching the firelight, the serpents flexing along both raised arms while she wound the tail through itself, took the silk from her teeth, and bound it all off in a high, tight ponytail with a soldier's knot.
Not one second of it was hurried, and not one second of it released his eyes.
The Venomborne Terror sat astride him, bare, and truly battle ready at last.
"...Now that," said Quinlan from the floor, with deep respect, "is how you declare a war."
"I already told you," replied Black Fang slowly. "Stop speaking nonsense."
She rose up on her knees, reached down, grabbed his length with zero tenderness, and set him against herself.
"Black Fang."

Quinlan's voice stopped her at the exact point of contact. The amusement had gone out of it. She looked down and found him serious for the second time that night, and underneath the seriousness, warm.
"Are you sure about this? I'm not a decision you can take back."
She held his eyes.
Then she answered him, without a speech, without an oath, without a single decoration.
She sank.

She took him in one slow, unflinching descent, and only two things in the world betrayed what it cost her: a single hitch of breath through her nose, and her hand, which shot down and closed around his forearm with crushing force, no caress anywhere in it, just the exact grip she had used once before, in a freezing cell, holding the only railing in reach.

Heat swallowed him, scalding and tight, a slow pulse he could count her heartbeat by, and the discovery of how warm she ran on the inside, this woman who greeted the world by pouring cold into it, emptied his head of every thought he owned.
Only one came back.
He was inside Black Fang.

Months of pursuing this breathtaking, unique woman, the wager, every wall she had ever raised between them, all of it had led to this: she had chosen him herself, climbed on, and taken him in. No victory on a bloody battlefield could ever compare to what he was feeling right now.
'Finally,' he thought, from the very bottom of his soul. 'Finally.'
Yet despite his joy, Quinlan was completely still beneath her.

He did not thrust, did not tease, did not say one word about the vise on his forearm. He just lay there, patient as bedrock, and let her arrive at her own pace, and the only movement in him was his free hand, which came to rest, light as snowfall, on her knuckle.
Black Fang stared down at him. Her eyes closed once, slowly, opened again, and the wariness at the very bottom of them had thawed by a degree.
Then Quinlan's gaze dropped to where their bodies joined, and stopped there.

A thin line of red was working its way down. Her first blood, four hundred years signing its own certificate, and at the sight of it every trace of the spectator left his face. Concern surfaced instead, plain and unhidden, and his lips parted.

The word never got out. Black Fang let go of his forearm, leaned down over him, and pinned both his wrists to the floor on either side of his head, her weight arriving through straight arms, her eyes one hand-span above his and forbidding the subject.
He did not test the hold even once, but... "Does it hurt?" he asked anyway.
The scoff came out flat as ever, but on the way to it her teeth caught her lower lip for half a heartbeat, there and gone.
"Stop treating me like a fragile maiden. This is nothing." Her fingers flexed on his wrists. "And we are in the middle of a duel of great importance. Have you forgotten?"
Her face was perfectly grave about it.
"Isn't it natural to be concerned for the woman I love?" Quinlan asked from the floor, making no bid for his hands back. "I can't help myself. It's instinctive."
For a long moment nothing in her moved, and then the fingers around his wrists lost a fraction of their pressure without her permission.

She had a counter ready for every weapon he had shown all night, yet she had nothing for that sentence. So she answered with the only thing she owned: her hands crushed back down on his wrists, her weight came forward, and she began to move.
"...Then restrain your instincts," she said, one full beat too late. "Or you'll be supplying the woman you love with your sad little pills for eternity."

chapters.title: Chapter 1856 Fierce Duel
paragraphs: "...Then restrain your instincts," she said, one full beat too late. "Or you'll be supplying the woman you love with your sad little pills for eternity."
Black Fang rode Quinlan on the floor of the wrecked dawn dojo, his wrists pinned to the boards on either side of his head, and within a few heartbeats it became clear that she had brought a doctrine.
She fought sex the way she fought everything, as a discipline to be conquered, and she had spent one entire night gathering intelligence from a windowsill.

The opening sequence arrived exactly as drilled: a measured roll of the hips copied beat for beat from her sister's counter-tempo, an angle she had watched him enjoy earlier in the night and now reproduced from memory with a genius combatant's precision.
It worked for four beats.
"...Amazing," said Quinlan, with sincerity.
Being inside this precious woman was simply otherworldly.
*Creak.* Under her grip, his pinned right hand strained against the boards hard enough to make the wood complain, and the tremor of it arrived straight up her arm.
Her eyes logged both tells as direct hits, one from his mouth, one delivered into her own palm. She struck the same seam again, and her own body defected mid-stroke.
The stolen angle turned out to carry a second edge on her side of the blade.
It dragged across a place inside her that no surveillance had mapped, and her proud rhythm stumbled as her own hips answered him without authorization from anyone.
The first sound made it no further than her teeth. Strangled at the border. Her expression declared a clerical error and resumed operations.
She resumed at half speed, and the duel entered its research phase.

Her first experiments demanded her hands back within three strokes. She released his wrists one wary finger at a time, watching for rebellion, and the freed hands rose, considered their liberty, and returned to her thighs, exactly where she had left them. The ruling held.

She tested in increments. A centimeter of change per pass, a new angle every third stroke, pausing at each discovery to catalogue what it did to him and, with visibly mounting insult, what it did to her. She rode him, attentive, flinching at nothing, her brow knit in quiet strategy while her own nerves kept defecting to the enemy.

His hands helped where the law allowed. Steadying her hips through a wobble, warm thumbs smoothing along whatever trembled, adjustments so small they never once touched her precious tempo, and every time a tremor ran her thighs he read it and eased her through it without comment.
The second sound got further.
Short, low, out the gate before the guard could close it. Her eyes widened a fraction at her own voice, betrayed by an instrument that had not failed her once in her life.
"Don't," she said.
"I said nothing."
"Yet."
"I was merely enjoying this wonderful view. Far be it from me to mock you for also enjoying yourself."
She studied his face for the lie and could not locate it, which was worse, and went back to work with her ears faintly dark at the rims.
It was three discoveries later that she looked at him, really looked, and the ledger hit a page it could not turn.
He lay easy against the cushion, one palm warm on her thigh, the other on her waist, watching her. That was all.

And there was nothing in his face she had a file for, because she had surveilled this man for long months and knew his whole repertoire: the performer, the tactician, the patient sadist, the duelist who ate masterpiece strikes as a form of courtship. Technique, all of it, layered and running.

Nothing was running now. The man beneath her lay in the wreck of a conquered dojo with a virgin terror learning to ride him by trial and error, at her speed, under her rules, and he was comfortable. At ease in a way none of her surveillance had once recorded, and she could not explain it.
She was still staring at him when her rhythm drifted, and she caught herself planning.

Her eyes went distant in the firelight, three new approaches drafting themselves behind the violet, a war college of one convening on top of him, bare and wet-thighed and absolutely absorbed in strategy.
The war college adjourned almost immediately, having produced nothing.
All three approaches, held up to the light, turned out to be the same approach.
Move your butt faster.

Beneath her Quinlan stayed untroubled, openly enjoying her, and every instinct she owned read that ease as provocation, because a confident opponent in a battle of this weight demanded a better answer than the one she was giving.
So did she simply... ride him harder? Would that even help turn the tide?
She reached for the next technique and found nothing where it should have been. Her entire close-quarters arsenal was severely lacking against the opponent she was fighting, Black Fang realized.
Her rhythm wavered a second time.
She sat very straight on him, filled and going nowhere, gaze dropping to his face and bouncing away, and her hands opened and closed against his chest as if reloading a bow she did not have.
Quinlan watched the campaign stall from below.

He watched her run out of plan mid-stride, hips holding their stubborn drilled cadence because nothing had countermanded it yet, and when her eyes came down to his... He saw a truly incredible sight. The big bad terror, Miss Venomborne herself, the most badass woman on the continent, suddenly awfully resembled a...
'Lost kitten in full battle armor. How utterly adorable.'
Something behind Quinlan's ribs went down without a fight. There was no counter in him, no read on her openings, no next move loading.
He loved this woman.
He wanted, with a want that outranked the duel, to make this simply good for her.
And there was no accomplishing that lying down.
She registered his hands only when the movement was already finished, palms sliding off her thigh and waist and taking her by the butt, both hands, the grip already set.
Terror went through her, real terror, colder than anything her capture or the ensuing torture sessions could ever have produced.
Four hundred years of sharpened instinct, and hands, moving far too slowly, had reached her body unseen, in close quarters, in the most important battle of her life.
She knew a billion counters for a grip like this and had time for none of them.
"Come here," he murmured, to a woman with nowhere closer to go.
He rose to a seated position, taking his time, nothing in it of the explosion she was expecting, and his eyes stayed on hers the whole way up.
Gravity took over, sliding her down the new angle and driving him deeper than any of her experiments had dared to go, and the third sound got out whole.
Low, short, unmistakable, and gone before she could kill it, straight into the finger's width of air between their mouths.
His chest came against hers. One arm wrapped her waist, one hand spread between her shoulder blades, and the duel, whatever it had been until that second, changed shape inside his arms.
By the wall, a body stirred.

chapters.title: Chapter 1857 Conditions
paragraphs: Ayame surfaced one sense at a time, face down in ruined ritual silk, and the first report her body delivered was that everything ached in the specific way that meant everything had been wonderful.

She groaned and rolled off her front, flopping onto her side, one cheek against the cool boards, and her mouth had already begun loading a complaint about being stored on the floor like luggage when her nose came back online.
The hall was thick with it. Sex, hours deep, layered like incense in a shrine to something deeply disreputable.
'...Oh. Right.' The memory arrived in one warm flood. The sacred duel. The forfeit.
Quin had destroyed her, thoroughly and with ceremony, and her body was a signed confession that she had loved every second of it. She let her eyes slide shut again, at total peace with her ruin.
Then her ears caught up.
Wet, rhythmic, unhurried, and close. And riding over the top of them, a woman's breathing.
Ayame's eyes opened.
'That... the smell I can explain, but this... cannot be me.' She was right here. Doing none of that.
She turned her head slowly, careful not to let hope get ahead of her.
Her sister was making love in the firelight.
Being made love to. The distinction could wait.

Black Fang, the Venomborne Terror, the undefeated poker face of the Vesper Consortium, sat wrapped around Quinlan in the middle of the floor, bare, her high ponytail swaying with their rhythm, moving with him chest to chest while he rose into her from below. And on her upturned face, unguarded in the red light, lived an expression no bounty notice had ever managed to render.
Ayame's eyes went wide.

The commentary rose in her by pure reflex, a lifetime's arsenal of it, the teasing, the deductions, the celebration, the extortion material being minted by the second, all of it surging for the exit at once.
But then all of it stood down.

She pushed herself up on unsteady arms, dragged the silk around her shoulders, and slid backward until her spine found the wall. There she settled, knees drawn loosely up, wrapped in wrecked ceremony, and watched her big sister's first time with the biggest, softest grin her face had ever produced, and said nothing at all.
The couple in the firelight had a dispute in progress.
"You are not..." The words came apart between strokes and had to be reassembled. "...taking this seriously."
"But I am very serious."
"This is a duel." Her palms pushed at his shoulders. "Fight me with sincerity."
He stopped.
Hips and hands and breath went still together, for the first time since he had risen off the cushion, and the stillness went off in her nerves like an alarm.
Her body misread it and primed for a strike.
He looked at her instead, from one inch away, and she looked back, because meeting a threat's eyes was as natural to her as breathing.
It was a mistake.
She had spent a lifetime reading opponents at a glance, and she had never once failed to find the bottom of a man.
She found no bottom. The look went down and down, past want, past worship, into some black vault of devotion with no walls she could locate, and every fathom of it was pointed at her.
And the deep old animal in her, the one that had kept her alive through four centuries of poison and steel, finally identified the trap.
She had climbed, of her own will, into the arms of an immortal monster, and the monster's weapon was adoration.
Her body had shrugged off every toxin this continent had ever brewed, but against this attack it offered no resistance at all.
Then he smiled, so close the violet was the only color left in his world, and the smile changed nothing underneath.
"I am as sincere as I ever could be."
He kissed her.
She went rigid inside his arms, both hands locked on his shoulders, every doctrine she owned scrambling for a protocol on a front no enemy had ever opened. None came.
So she fought the kiss.
For three full seconds the most feared mouth on the continent stayed sealed shut, eyes open, glaring at him from a range of zero, and he stayed, patient as weather, kissing the locked gate of her.
Her glare lost focus first.

Then her eyes closed, both traitors in the same instant, and her breath went next, surrendering through her nose in one long shiver, and last of all her mouth, the final garrison, opened under his and answered, unpracticed.
Her fingers slid up into his hair without any order being issued anywhere in her.

His state of being, his emotions, arrived through the seal of their mouths like heat through steel plate, sincerity at a dose nothing in her body knew how to neutralize, and she had nowhere at all to put this.
And it just kept coming!
Somewhere behind her ribs a rampart shifted on its foundations, and she made a sound into his mouth that no torturer had ever pulled out of her.
Then his arms moved, and the last distance died.
The duel, as far as Quinlan was concerned, had already concluded. Or, to be more accurate, had never existed.

The woman in his arms belonged to him now, at a depth no wager could reach, his to hold and guard and cherish for as long as forever ran, and every gram of pressure in his hold was telling her so, gently, one heartbeat at a time. He would level kingdoms over this woman.
The man holding her naked body was a terrible psychopath, a possessive calamity no mortal should ever have tried to duel, she realized.
The kiss broke by a millimeter, her breath undone in the space between their mouths.
"...Monster," she got out.
"Yeah." The agreement came immediate, warm, untroubled, his lips still touching hers. "I know."
What followed was tender, and it was a slaughter.

He moved into her unhurried and thorough, sure of every second, one hand splayed at the small of her back to steer the angle, the other cradling the back of her head, working her through each tremor instead of past it.

When a wave rocked her he rode it with her and eased her down its far side. When her breathing snagged he slowed until it found itself. He fought nothing. He simply attended, with all of himself, to the woman coming apart in increments against his chest.
*Pap. Pap. Pap.*

The sounds of them had gone soft and wet and regular, and her voice was surfacing between them now whether she permitted it or not, low broken pieces of it, "...ah. ...Hah. ...nn," each one arriving whole and being disowned on arrival.
"You don't need to hold back. I swear I won't ridicule you," Quinlan mentioned against her neck, biting and kissing all at once.
"Silence."
He did just as she hissed.

But her body kept climbing, and that was the front her doctrine had no page for. Each wave crested higher than the last, gathering toward an edge she had no name for, and at the top of every crest, right where it should have paid out, it went hollow instead.
The wave collapsed unpaid, the climb restarted from a higher floor, and her fingers dug deeper into his shoulders each time with mounting, furious confusion.
Quinlan felt it happen. He felt her reach the edge and get robbed at it, three times running, and a lesser man would have taken it for a review of his work.
He read the fine tremble in her thighs instead, the bafflement rising behind the violet, the body wound one turn past what any body should hold.
"Remind me," he breathed at her ear, never slowing. "When you win. What do I owe you?"
"The pills." Instant, even wrecked. "Every three days. For..."
"Mm. And you win when, exactly?"
Silence, of a very specific density.
Her rhythm stumbled.
'Wait... Conditions...' Her heart began climbing.
'What were the conditions?!'
Behind her eyes, at speed, the night's negotiation replayed itself in full: the standoff, the calculations, the syllogism, the undressing, every clause of it turned over twice in half a second.
"I forgot to set the conditions..." she realized with a low, disbelieving gasp.

The woman who did not enter a room without an exit, let alone a wager without conditions, had stripped, mounted the opposing party, and impaled herself upon him without once defining how the duel could be won.

Right.' The memory arrived in one warm flood.
The sacred duel.
The forfeit.
Quin had destroyed her, thoroughly and with ceremony, and her body was a signed confession that she had loved every second of it.
She let her eyes slide shut again, at total peace with her ruin.
Then her ears caught up.
Wet, rhythmic, unhurried, and close.
And riding over the top of them, a woman's breathing.
Ayame's eyes opened.
'That... the smell I can explain, but this... cannot be me.' She was right here.
Doing none of that.
She turned her head slowly, careful not to let hope get ahead of her.
Her sister was making love in the firelight.
Being made love to.
The distinction could wait.

Black Fang, the Venomborne Terror, the undefeated poker face of the Vesper Consortium, sat wrapped around Quinlan in the middle of the floor, bare, her high ponytail swaying with their rhythm, moving with him chest to chest while he rose into her from below.
And on her upturned face, unguarded in the red light, lived an expression no bounty notice had ever managed to render.
Ayame's eyes went wide.

The commentary rose in her by pure reflex, a lifetime's arsenal of it, the teasing, the deductions, the celebration, the extortion material being minted by the second, all of it surging for the exit at once.
But then all of it stood down.
She pushed herself up on unsteady arms, dragged the silk around her shoulders, and slid backward until her spine found the wall.
There she settled, knees drawn loosely up, wrapped in wrecked ceremony, and watched her big sister's first time with the biggest, softest grin her face had ever produced, and said nothing at all.
The couple in the firelight had a dispute in progress.
"You are not..." The words came apart between strokes and had to be reassembled.
"...taking this seriously."
"But I am very serious."
"This is a duel." Her palms pushed at his shoulders.
"Fight me with sincerity."
He stopped.
Hips and hands and breath went still together, for the first time since he had risen off the cushion, and the stillness went off in her nerves like an alarm.
Her body misread it and primed for a strike.
He looked at her instead, from one inch away, and she looked back, because meeting a threat's eyes was as natural to her as breathing.
It was a mistake.
She had spent a lifetime reading opponents at a glance, and she had never once failed to find the bottom of a man.
She found no bottom.
The look went down and down, past want, past worship, into some black vault of devotion with no walls she could locate, and every fathom of it was pointed at her.
And the deep old animal in her, the one that had kept her alive through four centuries of poison and steel, finally identified the trap.
She had climbed, of her own will, into the arms of an immortal monster, and the monster's weapon was adoration.
Her body had shrugged off every toxin this continent had ever brewed, but against this attack it offered no resistance at all.
Then he smiled, so close the violet was the only color left in his world, and the smile changed nothing underneath.
"I am as sincere as I ever could be."
He kissed her.
She went rigid inside his arms, both hands locked on his shoulders, every doctrine she owned scrambling for a protocol on a front no enemy had ever opened.
None came.
So she fought the kiss.
For three full seconds the most feared mouth on the continent stayed sealed shut, eyes open, glaring at him from a range of zero, and he stayed, patient as weather, kissing the locked gate of her.
Her glare lost focus first.

Then her eyes closed, both traitors in the same instant, and her breath went next, surrendering through her nose in one long shiver, and last of all her mouth, the final garrison, opened under his and answered, unpracticed.
Her fingers slid up into his hair without any order being issued anywhere in her.

His state of being, his emotions, arrived through the seal of their mouths like heat through steel plate, sincerity at a dose nothing in her body knew how to neutralize, and she had nowhere at all to put this.
And it just kept coming!
Somewhere behind her ribs a rampart shifted on its foundations, and she made a sound into his mouth that no torturer had ever pulled out of her.
Then his arms moved, and the last distance died.
The duel, as far as Quinlan was concerned, had already concluded.
Or, to be more accurate, had never existed.

The woman in his arms belonged to him now, at a depth no wager could reach, his to hold and guard and cherish for as long as forever ran, and every gram of pressure in his hold was telling her so, gently, one heartbeat at a time.
He would level kingdoms over this woman.
The man holding her naked body was a terrible psychopath, a possessive calamity no mortal should ever have tried to duel, she realized.
The kiss broke by a millimeter, her breath undone in the space between their mouths.
"...Monster," she got out.
"Yeah." The agreement came immediate, warm, untroubled, his lips still touching hers.
"I know."
What followed was tender, and it was a slaughter.

He moved into her unhurried and thorough, sure of every second, one hand splayed at the small of her back to steer the angle, the other cradling the back of her head, working her through each tremor instead of past it.
When a wave rocked her he rode it with her and eased her down its far side.
When her breathing snagged he slowed until it found itself.
He fought nothing.
He simply attended, with all of himself, to the woman coming apart in increments against his chest.
*Pap.
Pap.
Pap.*

The sounds of them had gone soft and wet and regular, and her voice was surfacing between them now whether she permitted it or not, low broken pieces of it, "...ah. ...Hah. ...nn," each one arriving whole and being disowned on arrival.
"You don't need to hold back.
I swear I won't ridicule you," Quinlan mentioned against her neck, biting and kissing all at once.
"Silence."
He did just as she hissed.
But her body kept climbing, and that was the front her doctrine had no page for.
Each wave crested higher than the last, gathering toward an edge she had no name for, and at the top of every crest, right where it should have paid out, it went hollow instead.
The wave collapsed unpaid, the climb restarted from a higher floor, and her fingers dug deeper into his shoulders each time with mounting, furious confusion.
Quinlan felt it happen.
He felt her reach the edge and get robbed at it, three times running, and a lesser man would have taken it for a review of his work.
He read the fine tremble in her thighs instead, the bafflement rising behind the violet, the body wound one turn past what any body should hold.
"Remind me," he breathed at her ear, never slowing.
"When you win.
What do I owe you?"
"The pills." Instant, even wrecked.
"Every three days.
For..."
"Mm.
And you win when, exactly?"
Silence, of a very specific density.
Her rhythm stumbled.
'Wait...
Conditions...' Her heart began climbing.
'What were the conditions?!'
Behind her eyes, at speed, the night's negotiation replayed itself in full: the standoff, the calculations, the syllogism, the undressing, every clause of it turned over twice in half a second.
"I forgot to set the conditions..." she realized with a low, disbelieving gasp.

The woman who did not enter a room without an exit, let alone a wager without conditions, had stripped, mounted the opposing party, and impaled herself upon him without once defining how the duel could be won.

chapters.title: Chapter 1858 Black Fang Goes All Out!
paragraphs: The price of victory - the pills - was real, but not one word had been spoken about what winning looked like, or losing, or who would judge it.
The first to orgasm? The first to be unable to continue? Something else?
Nothing was discussed.
Her eyes came back into focus one inch from his, and found him already watching her, warm and terrible.
"You knew," she said.
"Did I~?"
"You said nothing."
"You were the one who wanted to 'fight' me so bad." A long, deep stroke rolled through her mid-glare. "I merely obliged. You can't blame me."

The look she aimed at him would have opened throats in any other room. Delivered from the crest of his pace, naked, trembling, arms locked around his neck and voice in pieces, it lost a certain amount of edge in transit.
"You're speaking as if the entire duel was an excuse from me."
"Well..." Quinlan's grin arrived, and for the very first time, Black Fang's heart skipped a beat at the sight of it. "It wasn't me who demanded to have sex without conditions."
"Nothing changes," she managed through sheer grit. "The duel proceeds. I'll have you admit defeat."
"Sure," he nodded at her, going back for a kiss.
"Wipe that..."
He hooked one arm under her and rose into her, unhurried and total, and the sentence lost all its staff.
And she was losing. She knew forty ways to kill the man inside her and not one way to slow him down.

Her body was being carried to a beat she had not set, toward an edge she had not chosen, and the last clock in the hall that still ran on her time was losing minutes with every single push of his manhood into her core.
Prey.
The word rose from some old, old place in her and detonated.
That was what she had become in these arms: consumed, cherished, carried.
A meal that moaned.
"I refuse this fate!"

Her pride arrived all at once, every year of it, and the woman who had never once been anyone's anything decided, with her last unclaimed heartbeat, that she would rather die fighting than finish the night as his dinner.
Her palm hit his sternum with her full, unretouched strength, and the dawn dojo lost more heritage as Quinlan went flat, the boards under his back splitting in a spray of ancient lacquer.
*Krakk!*
The heat of the brazier leaned sideways.
It came off the coals and it did not rise; it bent toward the floor, toward her, and the shadows on the weapon racks stretched out after it.

Along her arms the serpent tattoos woke and began to move, coils winding down muscle gone taut, streaming toward her hands, and the violet of her eyes flooded outward from the pupils in rings until only slivers of white survived at the corners.
By the wall, the silk slid off one shoulder as the spectator sat up straight.
[Eternal Hunger] had come to the table.
She came down over him and pinned his wrists to the boards, exactly where the battle had started, and this time the hold was no doctrine. It was a kill-grip.

The spell poured everything it had into its keeper. Power crashed through the serpent coils into muscle and sinew, strength the cage had never released for anything less than war. She rode him at war pace, bare and blazing above him, her high ponytail snapping with the rhythm now instead of swaying, hellbent on pounding the primordial breeding machine beneath her into submission.
"Hah...! ...Nn...!" The war pace was hammering the sounds out of her now, and she disowned every single one mid-flight.
Quinlan did not counter it.
His hands turned over inside her grip, slow, unhurried, asking for nothing, and laced their fingers through hers.
Her pin became, without her permission, holding hands.
She bore down with killing weight. His thumbs brushed across her knuckles, twice, tenderly, as if she had reached for him first.
So she committed her reserves. She took his mouth.

Seal and siege, his own weapon returned to sender, the front no enemy had ever opened now flung wide from her side, and she kissed him as she had been kissed, every technique she owned now one kiss old.
The most feared woman on the continent was kissing him like a killing blow, and beneath her the man on the receiving end sighed into it, happy.
"...Perfection," he said into her mouth, with total sincerity.
Her rhythm stuttered. She resented it enormously, and attacked harder.
It made no difference.

Her assault broke over him at full power and moved him not at all. He did not strain against the pin, did not gather himself, did not so much as brace. And when she bore down to grind what was left of him into the boards, she made the same mistake twice in one night: she looked into his eyes.
They were far too honest.
"You are incredible," Quinlan said.
Her hips faltered.

"I look at you and I just can't help but smile with pride." His voice came up at her from inside her own pin, low and warm and completely unarmored. "You hung in their chains. In agony, over a secret that kept us safe, and you gave them nothing. Not a name. Not a tear. You are far too tough."
"I told you many times...!" It came out with half its usual authority, and none by the end. "Be silent..."
"You came here to outduel a primordial in a type of combat you never experienced before. And you're still trying to win right now. I adore that so much I can't put it into words."
Her war pace was dying under her and she could not find the order that used to prevent such things.
On her arms the serpent coils were slowing, the violet ebbing back toward her pupils, and her grip on his pinned wrists had stopped being a pin at all and become something that held on.

"And the way you love." His eyes never left hers. "You think nobody sees it. You stood behind Ayame when it counted and hugged her in front of everyone. You pulled a child out of a slaughtered village and sharpened her into Vex the Hexblade, and she would die for you, and you would die for her, and you would sooner hang in those chains again than say one word of it aloud."
"Stop." It arrived as a pleading whimper.
"And you are so, so beautiful. I simply can't get enough of merely looking at you. Truly. What a breathtaking sight you are, Black Fang."
Her mouth, the mouth that had held its line against torturers, began to turn downward at the corners, and she could not correct it.
Her heart was awake.

All of it, all at once, feeling more in one minute than she had allowed herself in centuries, with no training for any of it, and her hips had gone still without her noticing, and the hall was very quiet.
His hands slid free of her slackened grip, and she let them go.

They came up to her face and cupped it, both palms, thumbs resting on her cheekbones where they had rested on her knuckles, and Quinlan looked up at the woman above him with a fondness that had no bottom, and his voice dropped low and deep, for her and no one else.
"You've truly done your best all this time, haven't you?"
She broke then and there.

chapters.title: Chapter 1859 A Good Woman
paragraphs: She broke then and there.

The tears came all at once, hot and disbelieving, spilling over his thumbs, and the sob that followed had waited so long inside her that it came out small and wrecked, like it had forgotten its own shape on the way up.
Ayame's hand came up over her own mouth. Her eyes filled, and she stayed exactly where she was, because this was not hers to interrupt.

Quinlan drew Black Fang down, gently, out of the ruin of her pin and into his arms, one hand cradling the back of her head, the other spread warm across her back, and she went, all of her, no resistance left anywhere in her body.
Her face found the hollow of his neck.
And there, hidden from the firelight, hidden from the hall, hidden from every eye that had ever watched her for weakness, Black Fang nodded.
They stayed that way for a while, her tears cooling against his collarbone, his heartbeat arriving against her chest through both their ribs, slow and enormous and certain.
Then...
"Let me make love to you, Black Fang."
Long silence answered his words, followed by an even smaller, weaker second nod.
Quinlan hugged her tight and began to move again.
Slow and deep, nothing of the duel left anywhere in it.
The moan came out of her whole and unfought, given freely into his neck.
The border guard had stood down. The sounds followed one after another now, low and open and entirely hers, and she made no effort to suppress them.
"Can I..." she whispered, and Quinlan didn't even wait for her to finish her question.
"Yes."

She moved her limbs to hold him. Arms, legs, breath, every inch of her wound around every inch of him, tight and then tighter, clinging like the world would end the moment she let go. Quinlan wrapped her in both arms and gave her wave after patient wave, and the crest that had been robbed all night began to climb one final time with nothing standing in its road.
At the top of it he pressed his mouth to her ear.
"Whatever you need, the answer is yes. It'll always be yes."
And he stopped holding anything back.
"...Kh." One raw sound escaped him, his arms locking until her ribs creaked, and even going under, the duelist in her logged it: a direct hit, at last.

He finished without restraint, flooding into her womb at full primordial potency, and low on her belly the Beloved mark lit up through sweat and firelight as [Blessed Seed] crashed headlong into [Eternal Hunger].
The world hitched.
In a freezing cell she had taken what he gave her, and it had been enough to keep her breathing, and she had closed the account there, because breathing was all she had ever needed anything to do.
This was a different order of transaction.

Heat erupted through her from the inside, heat where there had only ever been cold, and the hunger that had gnawed at the bottom of her for as long as she had memories rose up to devour what was pouring in, and gorged, and gorged, and then, for the first time in its long ruinous life, stopped.
Sated.
Nothing anywhere in it that still wanted.
The quiet it left behind was so vast and so foreign that her whole body forgot what it was doing.
And what it was doing was standing at the top of the highest crest of the night, with no thief left anywhere on the summit.
She went over.
The finish took her like an avalanche takes a mountainside, total and long.

Her back bowed, her breath left in one unguarded rush, her arms crushed around his neck. The woman who had never lost anything came, and came, and could not stop coming, surge after surge through a body with no hunger left in it to eat the pleasure before it reached her, feeling all of it, undefended.
She did not hold through it. For the first time in her long life she did not even try.
The cry she gave up to the rafters was long and open and broken, and she clung to him through every last wave of it and hid none of it.
If any ancestor was watching the hall, she no longer cared.

A long time later, or what felt like it, Black Fang sat in his arms, trembling in fine, continuous detail, staring at the man her hands were braced against, her eyes gone back to their ordinary lethal violet and her face wearing an expression no living being had ever seen on it.
Confusion.
Total, catastrophic confusion, on a poker face with nothing left to hide behind.
Quinlan said nothing at all, only tucked one loose strand of hair behind her ear, which was somehow the most outrageous thing he had done all night, and let her stare.
By the wall, the biggest grin in the hall had gone wet at the edges, and its owner kept her historic silence.
Deep in the night, long after the brazier had banked itself down to embers and the breathing on his chest had gone soft and defenseless, the ruined silk by the wall began to rustle.
Quinlan turned his head. Ayame was padding toward him across the wreckage on her knees, cocoon and all, eyes half-lidded with sleep and absolute purpose.
She reached his free side, lifted his arm by the wrist, deposited herself against his ribs, and pulled the arm back down over her like a blanket she had ordered in advance.
He looked down at her. She looked up at him. Over the woman sleeping between them, two grins met in the dark and understood each other completely. Not one sound passed; the silence held.
A thumbs up rose slowly out of the silk. It was answered with equal ceremony.
And Black Fang, guardian to everyone and guarded by no one for almost her entire life, slept on until morning, watched over by the two grinning idiots who loved her far too much.
Dawn came up gray and slow past the veranda, finding the dawn dojo in a state its ancestors would have needed several generations of counseling to process.
Broken heritage lay where it had fallen. The cracks and stains in the floorboards were not going anywhere.
The light strengthened by degrees, gray giving way to pale gold across the wrecked boards.
Duty waited at the edge of Quinlan's mind, patient as a debt: the capital, the war of paper, the promise he had made to a king.
It could have him soon enough.
The woman asleep on his chest had waited her whole long life for one safe morning, and he was not going to be the man who cut it short.
It was well into the morning when she finally stirred.
She woke completely and at once, no fog, no swimming up.
One breath she was gone, and the next the violet was open and aimed at him, running its automatic accounting of exits and threats and angles.
The accounting found nothing to report. Only a man, still grinning, and a little sister beaming back on his other shoulder.
The scoff came, as it always did, and for the first time in its long career it carried no teeth at all.
With the legendary night in Fujimori lands concluding, it was time to move on.
There was much to do.

Confusion.
Total, catastrophic confusion, on a poker face with nothing left to hide behind.
Quinlan said nothing at all, only tucked one loose strand of hair behind her ear, which was somehow the most outrageous thing he had done all night, and let her stare.
By the wall, the biggest grin in the hall had gone wet at the edges, and its owner kept her historic silence.
Deep in the night, long after the brazier had banked itself down to embers and the breathing on his chest had gone soft and defenseless, the ruined silk by the wall began to rustle.
Quinlan turned his head.
Ayame was padding toward him across the wreckage on her knees, cocoon and all, eyes half-lidded with sleep and absolute purpose.
She reached his free side, lifted his arm by the wrist, deposited herself against his ribs, and pulled the arm back down over her like a blanket she had ordered in advance.
He looked down at her.
She looked up at him.
Over the woman sleeping between them, two grins met in the dark and understood each other completely.
Not one sound passed; the silence held.
A thumbs up rose slowly out of the silk.
It was answered with equal ceremony.
And Black Fang, guardian to everyone and guarded by no one for almost her entire life, slept on until morning, watched over by the two grinning idiots who loved her far too much.
Dawn came up gray and slow past the veranda, finding the dawn dojo in a state its ancestors would have needed several generations of counseling to process.
Broken heritage lay where it had fallen.
The cracks and stains in the floorboards were not going anywhere.
The light strengthened by degrees, gray giving way to pale gold across the wrecked boards.
Duty waited at the edge of Quinlan's mind, patient as a debt: the capital, the war of paper, the promise he had made to a king.
It could have him soon enough.
The woman asleep on his chest had waited her whole long life for one safe morning, and he was not going to be the man who cut it short.
It was well into the morning when she finally stirred.
She woke completely and at once, no fog, no swimming up.
One breath she was gone, and the next the violet was open and aimed at him, running its automatic accounting of exits and threats and angles.
The accounting found nothing to report.
Only a man, still grinning, and a little sister beaming back on his other shoulder.
The scoff came, as it always did, and for the first time in its long career it carried no teeth at all.
With the legendary night in Fujimori lands concluding, it was time to move on.
There was much to do.

chapters.title: Chapter 1860 Voided Wager
paragraphs: Morning arrived in full over the Fujimori estate, and the pale gold coming off the snow garden found the dawn dojo looking like the site of a small, very thorough war.

In the middle of it, the night's survivors still lay in formation: Quinlan flat on his back, Black Fang stretched along his chest, and Ayame tucked in against his other shoulder, ruined ritual silk and all.
The scoff had barely finished leaving Black Fang's lips when the morning began filing the rest of its report.

A terribly cheeky little sister was watching her from across the man's collarbones, chin propped on her stacked hands, wearing a grin that ran from one ear clean over to the other and had settled in for a long occupancy.

The man himself was looking at her too, yet, to her surprise, was not wearing a grin of victory. What decorated his was a mild smile of sheer happiness, asking for nothing, mocking nothing, and his hand began moving along her naked shoulder in slow, soft passes.

Her waking accounting had checked for exits and threats and cleared the room. The second accounting arrived now, covering everything the first had never been trained to look for: bare, in daylight, in a wrecked sacred hall, arranged on top of a primordial, with an audience, being petted.
Black Fang went rigid from crown to heel.

She peeled his hand off her shoulder with two fingers, deposited it back on its owner, and was upright in the next motion, off him and marching, spine straight, for the pile her clothes had spent the night in.

Black Fang dressed through the surveillance as if the hall stood empty. Bindings wound tight, buckles closed in sequence, the needle-fine pins slid back into the seams they lived in, and at no point did she acknowledge the two pairs of eyes tracking every pass of her hands. Acknowledgment would have implied that something worth witnessing was occurring.
Ayame stayed curled against his side in the wreckage of last night's ritual silk, and her eyes never once left her sister.
Black Fang stood in the middle of the hall, immaculate.
Her hair was pinned high again, without one strand left loose as evidence. She had restored herself to factory condition while the other two were still negotiating with the concept of morning.
She surveyed them, then the hall. Then she issued her ruling to the room at large.
"A battle happened here last night." Flat, certain, a document being stamped. "That is the entirety of what occurred."
The violet moved from Quinlan to Ayame and back, slow and level, daring either witness to append one syllable to the record.
Quinlan nodded along agreeably. "Yeah. A duel of great importance. Nothing more, nothing less."
Ayame propped her chin on his chest.

She possessed, at that moment, the richest teasing portfolio any little sister had ever held. One entire legendary night of material. Sounds, sentences, a nod given twice. She took a long, visible moment to select.
"A settled battle. Understood~" Her eyes shone up at her big sister. "Although, for such simple accounting, you're checking our faces an awful lot to see whether we believe it."
The temperature in the hall dropped.
But no aura of pure dread followed. Black Fang instead elected to pretend a cheeky samurai brat did not exist in the room with her and Quinlan Elysiar.

"As for the wager itself." Black Fang proceeded to the next item on her docket. "No conditions of victory were ever defined. Where no conditions exist, no defeat can be recorded, and where no defeat exists, there is nothing to honor. The wager is void."
She stood braced, chin high, violet leveled at Quinlan, visibly loaded with prepared rebuttals for the appeal.
"Sure," said Quinlan.
The silence exceeded regulation length.
"You agree."
"Completely. No conditions, no verdict. Void it is." He slid his fingers into the hair of someone who did not exist in this room with the two of them, at peace with the universe.

Black Fang's eyes narrowed to needle width as she hunted for the trap. She had prepared for gloating. For refusal. For the insufferable grin and a counter-motion demanding arbitration. After all, she knew very well that if someone won last night's duel...
It wasn't her.
That's why a simple agreement appeared on none of her contingency sheets.
"...Good," she managed, one full beat too late.
Then Quinlan's pocket ring flashed.
A lacquered case arced across the hall. She caught it one-handed and had it open before it finished arriving.
Pearl-white pills sat inside in ordered rows. [Blessed Seed Pill]. Aurora's masterwork, the concentrate she had rationed her existence around for weeks, row after row after row of it. A full supply.
"Yours," said Quinlan. "If the wager is void, you'll need the pills."

The prize of the voided wager had been a delivery schedule: one pill, every twelve hours, for eternity, from his hand. The case now in her possession quietly abolished the schedule, and the visits, and the last operational reason attached to either.
Black Fang looked at it precisely as long as an inventory required.
"..." It vanished into her sleeve.
Both of them watched her stand there, her eyes aimed at Quinlan.
Her mouth opened. Nothing reported for duty. It closed again.
Somewhere behind the violet, an emergency session convened, found no precedent on file, and dissolved without a ruling.
She was truly, utterly, speechless.
She had no idea what to do now. No wager left to argue, no debt left to settle, no enemy anywhere in the room, and not one protocol in her entire arsenal for two people simply being good to her.
Then her body, the only department of her still taking orders, took over.
From one moment to the next, she was gone.
"She ran away..." Ayame giggled, purring, far too joyous, hugging Quinlan close for a long second. "My sister is a tsundere~"
"...Yeah," Quinlan agreed, not even trying to fight the grin down. "What a fucking adorable creature."
"I know right?!" Ayame sang, hugging him even tighter.
Silence descended for a few seconds, save for Ayame's happy humming. Quinlan used the time to conduct the official damage survey of the most sacred hall on Fujimori land.
Split boards at the center of the floor, radiating cracks, courtesy of a strike that had relocated him mid-duel. The inventory only got worse from there.
'We gave this place a proper trashing,' he concluded solemnly. 'Historic events demand historic evidence. Or something like that.'
Black Fang landed on the roof of the neighboring wing without a sound, and there her body finally consented to stop.
She crouched low and it took her a moment to notice she was shaking, breathing hard, heart slamming against her ribs like it was fighting its way out to go back inside.

Her hand went into her sleeve and came out with the lacquered case. She opened it. The pearl-white rows looked back, orderly, patient, worth more than any treasury on the continent, and his voice replayed over them in perfect fidelity.
'Yours. If the wager is void, you'll need the pills.'
She ran the words again. Then again. The meaning did not change on any pass.
She was unaging now, for any horizon that mattered. Not by schedule, not one pill at a time: a full case of her own, enough to put entire months between her and the word expiry.
Which meant...
She could leave with the next breath, disappear, do whatever pleased her for as long as it pleased her, and drop by every few months when the case ran low.
And he would refill it. Without one question, without one grievance, with that same mild smile that mocked nothing.
She was certain of it. She could predict the man now.
He had handed her the means to honor her own ruling, smiling.

Nobody, in four hundred years of careful accounting, had ever handed her anything without a price attached somewhere in the fine print. She had been discarded before she could properly walk, and every transaction since had billed her on the back end, and on that constant she had built her entire doctrine: everything given is collateral on something owed.
He had been holding the one leash that actually worked on her, yet now put it in her hands.
'Illogical... I don't understand him. Why do this?'
Without the wager, she did not have to stay.
That was what the case in her hand meant.
But.

chapters.title: Chapter 1861 Incomprehensible Man
paragraphs: Her gaze dropped. Her free hand was on her belly, palm flat over the mark.
The skin under it was warm. It had been warm since last night, a small hearth burning low in a body that had run cold for four centuries, and it would not bank down.
The violet began to swim.
Madness rose in it, the dangerous kind, with nowhere to point itself and no one to kill.

'I am free of time itself now,' she informed the mark, in full decree register. 'The one chain every mortal being wears, and mine is cut. Quinlan will tear the barrier down soon, and the restriction dies with it.'

'The whole world, open, for the first time in my life. I can leave whenever I please. Go wherever I please. Kill whatever I please. I ascended alone once, from nothing, and I require no one for a second ascent.'
She stared down at her own belly the way she stared at enemies she was about to kill.
The mark pulsed warm under her palm, unintimidated.
'...I do not want to?'
The breach was answered at once, with logic.

'The gains alone are decisive. Every kill mine, whole and unshared. No experience points distributed, no spoils split across an entire group. When the barrier breaks, I will grow as I grew as a girl. Alone is optimal. Alone is the proven track.'
The logic was flawless. The logic had always been flawless.
Her want ignored it entirely.
She tore the offending hand off her belly and planted it on the roof, where it could do no further harm.
*Krrk.*
The ridge tile under it broke through in five clean lines, one per finger.
Below the eaves, the estate's birds decided, unanimously, to be elsewhere.

'Why.' It came out in the voice she used on enemies needing information extraction, the voice no subject had ever held out against. 'Why do I not want it? Why does the optimal path hold no appeal? Why do I wish my kills witnessed? Why do I want to hunt beside him, when I have never once required anyone beside me? Answer!'
Along her forearms, the serpents stirred, coiling in slow unrest.
The subject declined to testify.
The voice that had never needed to ask twice asked twice.
Then a third time.
From the hall below, muffled by tile and distance, came the sound of two idiots collapsing into laughter.

The answer, when it arrived, did not come out of the interrogation. It drifted up from below, wrapped in laughter, and assembled itself out of the evidence unbidden: a gift with no invoice attached, a smile that mocked nothing, a leash placed into her own hands.
Only one hypothesis on record produced that pattern. She had never handled it herself, only read the reports.
'Love...' she murmured, violet swirling, comprehending nothing.
'Impossible. Infeasible. But what is it then?'
The most feared woman on the continent conducted a lengthy soul search on the Fujimori clan's rooftop.
And when she was done, she did not leave.
Kaede came walking up the estate's oldest courtyard with her head bowed and a stick of temple incense carried in both hands.

She had been waiting for this ever since the truth came out: a morning where she could come to the dawn dojo, kneel on the floor where she had committed the worst act of her life, and apologize to the ancestors properly, alone, expecting nothing back.

Every notable Fujimori was tested on that floor. Her father had first closed her hands around a practice grip there, six years old, winter light on the boards, his voice above her promising that the floor remembered everyone it had ever judged.
And years later, on the same boards, before the same ancestors, she had dueled her own sister for the succession, taken the verdict, and spent it on a slave contract.
Twenty paces from the doors, the dawn dojo giggled.
Kaede stopped walking.
The sound came again, doubled: a woman's giggle, bright and breathless and thoroughly undignified, wound around a man's lower laugh.

Her first theory was that some of the staff had chosen the clan's most sacred hall for a tryst, and that she would now have to determine whether a penitent in servant's gray had standing to discipline anyone for anything.
Then the giggle resolved into a voice, and the theory died on the spot. She had known that voice its whole life.
She should have turned around. She was telling herself as much the entire time her feet carried her to the doors.

The great doors of the dawn dojo stood wide open to the winter morning. Slid apart the night before, by hands that had owned every right to open them, and left that way since, because closing the most sacred doors of the clan had evidently made nobody's list of concerns.
She looked in.
The hall had been destroyed.
'The floor!' she began. 'The central boards have been... The lacquer is... The stains... the brazier was allowed to...'
The report failed to complete a single clause.

Her eyes kept moving anyway, from the split and cratered center of the sacred floor, across a dried dark tide staining a long stretch of heritage grain, to the weapon rack leaning drunk against its brothers, and nobody in the room had even noticed, let alone moved to do anything about it.
The two occupants lounged in the middle of the most sacred ground her clan owned as if ruins were furniture.
And then there was her sister.
'Hie?!'
Ayame Fujimori had been the measure Kaede spent her whole life failing to reach.

Perfect form in the practice yard at dawn; the heir who never slouched, never raised her voice, never let one hair fall out of place in front of the clan. She was grace, honor, and dedication welded into one small relentless person, the living argument that the Fujimori name meant what it claimed to mean.
Kaede had studied her the way other children studied scripture, right up until the months before her own great sin.
That sister was naked.
Naked, in the holiest hall of their line, sprawled the full length of a naked man, giggling into his neck while his hand rested on her bare backside with the confidence of territory long held.
Kaede got herself behind the doorframe.
'What??? Did I die? Am I dreaming?!' Kaede screamed inwardly.

She had no memory of ordering the movement; her body had simply removed her from the sightline and pressed her back flat against the outer wall, incense stick clutched to her chest. Her hands came up over her face.
Then her fingers opened a crack, because apparently her hands had come up for form's sake only.
She understood the situation completely. That was the worst part.
The man was Quinlan Elysiar, shamelessness given flesh and crowned for it, and the keeper of her sister's heart, as the entire continent knew by now.

And Ayame owed this clan nothing, much less respect. She had every right in existence to tell the Fujimori, their halls, their precepts, and their ancestors' floorboards to burn. Kaede herself had signed the deed to that right and collected payment for it.
All of this was rational.
Yet none of that helped.
'She... She had s-s-sex?! H-hard at that... In the sacred dojo?!'
Understanding a thing and watching it turned out to be two different organs, and the second one was failing.
'Wait.'
Kaede had a sudden realization.
The evidence of his crimes was clear: a destroyed room, and a sister whose behind was still slightly red. There were no enemies here. Which meant...
'Is he... beating her?!'
