chapters.title: Chapter 1891 Just That?
paragraphs: He looked at her then, truly looked, and the hall watched the Duke of Ravenshade take the full measure of his own executioner and find a footnote.

The first sound out of him was a cough. One dry spasm of disbelief, knocked loose rather than spoken, then another, and then Tharion Ravenshade threw back his head and laughed in the great hall of Vraven.
It rolled out of him in waves, enormous, unpracticed, doubling him over his own knees, the composure of a courtroom lifetime coming apart in front of six hundred witnesses.
"A BARONY!" He surfaced strangled, swiped at his eyes with one ringed hand, and went down again. "One dissolved border barony... a rounding error in a county ledger... THAT is what you are?"
His arm swept the wrecked case, the sealed floor, the throne, all of it.
"The audit! The trial! My house, my blood, my seat! All of it... All of it... over THAT?"

Iris had built this moment in the cage, brick by brick, down every year of the dark: the man at the top hearing her name, going white, understanding at last, in his final breath, exactly what was collecting him.
In all those years of building, she had never once laid a brick where he laughed.
'Hear that, Damian? Mom?' she thought, very quietly, into the place where her brother lived. 'We're funny.'
The old wound did what it always did.
It came up her spine as fire.
"'That' was my family."
Her voice had gone soft, and the whole hall leaned away from the soft.
The red of her eyes had begun to turn, red revolving within red.
"And you're laughing."
The laughter shut off.

"Yes," said the Duke of Ravenshade, and the humor burned out of his voice between one word and the next. "I am laughing. The renowned history of my house, undone over a stain a bailiff would not have crossed the road to collect."
His hands opened at his sides.
"I refuse it. I will not be ended by a NOTHING!"
The rings answered him first.
"[Attainder]."
Every stone on both his hands went from glitter to glare. Light climbed his arms in ropes as everything banked inside them woke together.
Then the rest of him arrived.

Pressure slammed outward across the hall, and the nearest banners tore off their poles. The marble under his boots split in a star. In the front rows, nobles went down without deciding to, and the great chandeliers swung groaning on their chains.
"He's about to go all out! Protect your children and wives!" somebody screamed in the front rows.
Level seventy-four.

The realm had been given generations to forget it, because the duke did his killing with clerks and seals ever since he reached that level and faced the same restriction all peak existences did on the continent.
The body under the velvet had climbed higher than almost any peer of this realm, and every rung of that climb was awake now, aimed at the girl with no house.
The duke's eyes went to the burning cut in his king's floor, and the courtroom in him priced it in one look.
"A hole in the ground," he said. "That is the whole of your office."
Across from the burning duke, Iris rolled her shoulders once, and her back caught fire.
She wasn't about to enter a verbal showoff with this scumbag when she could beat the fuck out of him instead.

The Bloodfather's sigil ignited between her shoulder blades, and its light bled straight through the plain cloth, a line of red-gold burning from her nape to the small of her back. The galleries behind her got the full length of it.
The mark drank deep from the Crimson Reservoir, and her class climbed and climbed, yet it was still going to leave her short of him.
But Iris Ravenclaw never cared about such a problem in her entire life.
Then she opened her hand at her side, and a second seam parted the air beside it, this one narrow as a coin slot. The cut in the floor stayed exactly where she had put it.
It was time to collect.
"[Tithe of the Guilty]."
[The Demon of Vengeance levies a special assessment upon all residents of hell.]
[Collection: 38/38.]
Down in the ember light, thirty-eight torments paid without stopping. The pillars kept climbing, the wire kept writing, the crucible kept pouring, and the levy came up out of all of it anyway.
[The sentence is not suspended for payment.]

What poured up out of the slot was coin: dull red metal, each piece stamped with a howling face, and the stamps were still howling. They snapped to her, sank hissing into her skin, and burned in along the line of the sigil.
Her class ate suffering, and thirty-eight of it had just been paid in.
"Coin from a pit," the duke sneered across the hall. "Even your power is stolen revenue."

The hall, the crown, the watching galleries, all of it fell out of her attention, and what was left standing in front of her was the last rung of the only ladder she had ever climbed: her father's ruin, her mother's price, Damian's terror.
They went at each other in the same breath.
The duke came like a bull, mad and overwhelming, a lifetime of amassed power spent in one straight line.
Iris went to meet him square, resolute, with not a single drop of evading intent in her at all, despite everyone knowing how many levels and stats he had on her.
"[Distraint]."
The duke's whole treasury came down the line of his arm and into one fist.
"Die!"
"[Torment Cycle]."
She said it into his charge, flat and bored, and planted both boots on the king's marble.
She got both arms up in front of her face, and his fist came through them anyway.
Her right forearm snapped inside the block. The break went up her arm as white heat, and the cycle swallowed every drop of it.
The rest was distance.
Her body crossed half the hall in one flat line, and the crown's ledger stacks detonated around her into a blizzard of loose paper.
She hit the marble, skidded through the wreckage of the evidence, and came to rest against an overturned stack with blood running from her mouth and her arm bent where arms do not bend.
"Her arm," a woman said in the middle rows, and put her hand over her mouth. "Her arm's bent the wrong-"
"Quiet," her husband told her, with no air behind it at all.
Tharion turned his back on her, on the sentence, on the throne itself, and walked for the great doors.
The cut in the floor lay next to him even still. He came up to its rim, looked down into the ember light for as long as a man looks at a puddle, and stopped there to call across it.
"Ravenshade! We are leaving."
By the doors, on the far side of the open hell, six men in his colors heard their duke call. Every one of them found the floor with his eyes and stayed exactly where the marshals had put them.
The duke's shoulders had just registered that silence when the laughter started.
It came low and wet through the blood, from right behind him. Iris Ravenclaw was in the air, lunging at him with her chin slick red, grinning wide enough to show bloody teeth.
"That's the hardest anyone's hit me since I was four."
The duke came around at the sound.
"[Cycle's End]."
She said it through her teeth, and every drop the cycle had swallowed came back up her spine and arrived in her good hand.
She punched.

chapters.title: Chapter 1892 Listless Demon
paragraphs: Her fist landed on his sternum, and the hall heard it. Deep and wet, the structural sound of a chest changing shape.
The blow lifted the Duke of Ravenshade off the floor of his king's hall.
"RAVENCLAW-" The name came out of him as a roar.
Her knuckles shattered on the way through. She felt it happen, somewhere far away, and ignored it like all the other pain.

She had the Bloodfather's buff, her class's buff, thirty-eight tithes paid in, and a broken arm banked on top of them. All of it together, and Iris Ravenclaw still could not kill Tharion Ravenshade with a punch.
But she was more than strong enough to move him two paces.
Right into the gates of hell.
He went over the rim backward, rings flaring defiantly, still fighting, and the ember light took him.
He struck the black metal of another world still roaring, and words wrote themselves across his sight, patient and courteous.
[Welcome to the hell of the Demon of Vengeance.]
"I will not be taken out like this!" [Attainder] flared, and the script burst apart like a struck fire. "Ravenclaw!"
Despite having been tossed into the gate, Tharion was still more than powerful enough to fight back, best evidenced by the fact he wasn't yet counted among hell's residents.
Iris tried to close the gate but she couldn't. Tharion was given the chance to escape until he was properly defeated.
So she opened her good hand.
"[Conscription]."
[The Demon of Vengeance conscripts all residents of hell.]
[Muster: 38/38.]
[Service is not compensated.]

The sigil down her spine reversed, and every coin her hell had ever paid her rained back down the cut, howling. The red of her eyes slowed, the color left her face, and she came down onto one knee at the rim, still spending.
The hall watched its executioner pay.
Below, thirty-eight bodies caught fire.

From every glowing district of her hell, his own machine came for him: Corvane pulled down off his pillar, hands cooked into climbing hooks, the chief clerk wrapped in cured sheets of his own written skin, the counts of the inner circle trailing pens from their opened wrists.
Thirty-eight residents, begging, weeping, and coming anyway.
"Stand down, you imbeciles!"
They apologized while their nails peeled the velvet off his arms.

He tore them apart faster than the domain could mend them, and the domain mended them anyway. Above, at the rim of the burning cut, six hundred nobles watched the most renowned duke of the realm drown in a pile of his own vassals.
They hit him as one burning body, because one will held every hand in it.

The Duke of Ravenshade went down under his own counts, his own clerks, his own collectors, roaring orders at the fire until the black metal closed over his ring-light. The last thing hell let him keep was the order half-finished in his mouth.

The seam breathed shut.
Paper was still settling across the great floor of Vraven.

The scarred marble, the torn banners, the wrecked stacks of the crown's evidence, all of it lay in absolute silence, and the flagstones where hell had been open were the only whole stones left in the hall.
And into that silence, her domain wrote the day's accounting where every noble in the kingdom could read it.
[Resident: 39.]
It was over.
Eighteen years of rungs. The dying scum, the syndicate lords, the false Covenant, the count, and now the man at the very top... Done.
Every debt collected, every name crossed out.
She opened her hand, and a seam the width of a palm parted the air in front of her, private, angled for her eyes alone.
Down in the ember light, on the far border of her domain, a fat shape hauled itself up a glowing pillar, one hand-span at a time, screaming.

The man who had priced her family. The man who had used her brother. And somewhere far below, the man who had orchestrated it all from the shadows. She stood in the seat of the nation with their eternity in her hand, and she watched them suffer.
She waited to feel it.
The warmth of thirty-nine coals sat banked in her chest, steady as a hearth.
And it warmed nothing.
'It's done,' she told the dark where her brother lived. 'I got all of them.'
The scream went on below, the pillar glowed, and the hall breathed behind her.
'...So why does everything weigh the same?'
Nobody had warned her about the end of the road. Nothing was waiting for her here.
The seam whispered shut, and she stood at the end of the only road she had ever known, with nowhere left to put one foot in front of the other.
A large, warm hand settled on her head.
It came from behind, unhurried, and it did not pat or ruffle. It just rested there, heavy and sure, the exact weight of the one person alive who had been in the basement with her.
"Feeling empty?" Quinlan asked.
Iris said nothing.
She stared at the sealed stones with her arms hanging at her sides, one of them still bent wrong, and the silence she gave him was the loudest yes the hall had ever heard.
He didn't take the hand away.
"Excuse me?"
The sound cut across the moment from five paces off: bright, offended, and profoundly unimpressed.
Ayame stood with her arms crossed and her head tilted, staring at Iris.
"I knew you were slow, but are you actually disabled? Have I been bullying a girl with special needs all this time?"

The samurai's voice climbed with sheer disbelief. "You stood in a burned record-house and made a creed out of it. You said you'll not stop until no child has to wait for help that never comes. Do you really think your work is done?"
Iris's head came up.
"...Watch your tone before I beat you up, you slit-eyed cunt."

"Sure, come at me~" Ayame's grin arrived, wicked and warm at once. "Thirty-nine tenants, and you think you're finished. Your hell has one shitty little village in it, you tragic landlord. There's a whole damned universe of deserving candidates out there, and you dare act listless?"

"She is right, you know," Lucille said warmly, drifting closer with the rest of the family, utterly at home on the royal floor. "The place looked quite spacious. It would be a shame to stop furnishing it."
"Group verdict~" Kitsara sang, five white tails swishing. "You're amazing, we love you, don't cry, and let's go ruin a billion more scumbags!"
"Cry?" Iris muttered dryly, and the word sat wrong in her own mouth. "Me?"
Then a blonde comet arrived.
Blossom had held herself back for as long as dogkin physics allowed, and that time was over. She planted herself directly in front of Iris, tail going, hands balled into determined fists.

"Iris is Blossom's good friend!" she declared, to Iris, to the hall, to the crown of Vraven, and every noble within earshot. "If Iris is sad, Iris should talk to Blossom! Blossom is a very good listener. Blossom listened to a whole trial today and only got confused four times!"
"...I'm not sad."
"Iris is about to start leaking," Blossom reported, pointing respectfully at Iris's face.
"I'm not!" Iris's hand came up and found her own cheek wet, and she stared at her fingers, utterly betrayed.
The girls did not laugh at her.

That was the remarkable thing, the thing a hall full of watching nobility would retell for years and completely fail to explain: the most dangerous group of women alive stood in a loose half-circle around one crying swordswoman, and every face in the circle was soft.
Quinlan's hand left a single light tap on her head. It said everything.
Then he stepped up beside her and swept his free arm out at the great hall, at the shaken peerage, at the banners, at the whole velvet-and-gold breadth of the kingdom.

"Look at all this, my partner in crime." The Primordial Villain's grin came down at her, villainous and fond in equal measure. "A continent of titles, and you've barely audited one duchy. I suspect even in Ravenshade you'll find a lot more of them. We have a long, long road ahead of us."
Partner.
The title went through Iris Ravenclaw like dawn through a shutter.

chapters.title: Chapter 1893 Pile Rights
paragraphs: Somewhere above the world, in patient ink, her class had already written it: the Villain and his justicar.
A road that did not end at the top of any ladder, because it did not end at all.
The emptiness was still there. But it had stopped being a wall and become room.
Room for the work, for the creed, and, apparently, for this pack of lunatics currently pretending they weren't all watching her cry.
Iris scoffed, wet and unconvincing, and looked away from all of them. "Take your hand off. I'm not a pet."
The hand stayed.
She did not move to remove it.

Her eyes were streaming freely now, and the smile had gotten past every guard she owned. She stood there scowling through both, a demon of vengeance leaking in front of the entire peerage of Vraven, radiantly, furiously happy.
"Iris!"
Armored weight hit her from the side.

Queen Felicity Valorian, crown clutched in one arm, had abandoned every shred of royal dignity and closed the distance at a sprint. Her hug arrived with the full sincerity of fourteen years and half a suit of plate.
"I'm so happy for you!" she wailed into Iris's shoulder, crying instantly, completely, without any negotiation at all. "You did it, you finally did it!"
"Gh... I just fought a level 74 enemy. All of you should take a step back and give me some damned room-"
"Pile rights!" Kitsara announced.
"Wait!" said Iris.
They did not wait.

Blossom hit her first, then Feng, and then the rest of the family arrived as one warm landslide, and the Demon of Vengeance, Keeper of Eternal Suffering, Scourge of the Vile, vanished under a shrieking pile of the most powerful women on the continent in front of six hundred members of the peerage.
"Get off- you're all fat as fuck- what do you bitches eat?!"
They didn't listen.
"Ah. I dropped the crown!" the queen of Vraven said, from inside the pile.
"Wait, let me try it on~" Kitsara purred.
"Nooo... You shouldn't...!"
"It looks good on you~" Seraphiel giggled.
"You try it too!"
"Sure!"
"Me next!" Aurora laughed.

While the girls passed the royal crown around, Iris hissed, yelped, and swore in language that made three heralds write formal complaints, and the pile only squeezed tighter. Her tears would not stop.
But she started to smile as well.
Her domain's thirty-nine coals went on burning in her chest, under the only thing that had ever been waiting on the other side of vengeance.
Family. It had been down here the whole time.
Off to the side of the pile, precisely one step too far away to be included and one step too close to be uninvolved, stood Black Fang.
She exchanged a dry look with Quinlan, who winked at her.
"Feel free to jump in."
The Venomborne Terror pointedly decided that he no longer existed.
It took a while for the pile to release its prisoner.

When it finally came apart, laughing and disheveled, one armored figure extracted herself from the middle of it, stood, and spent a solemn moment straightening a crown that she managed to get back after valiant, royal effort.
Then Queen Felicity Valorian looked across the hall at her father.

Alexios Valorian, former king of Vraven, had drifted back up the dais during the commotion and settled onto the high throne out of pure habit, the sword of state gathered back across his knees, watching his daughter's happiness from the most comfortable seat in the room.
Felicity marched to the foot of the dais.

She put her fists on her armored hips, tilted her head back to aim her entire fourteen years up at him, and addressed the most feared warrior-king in human history in the voice of a girl finding her brother in her room.
"Um. Excuse me? That's my chair."
Alexios looked down at her.
"...So it is," he said.
"If you're abdicating, then abdicate! Up, up!" She actually shooed him, with both gauntlets.
The old king rose from the throne of Vraven with the gravity of mountains, stepped aside, and gestured her past. The corner of his mouth had surrendered.
The hall watched their new queen climb the dais.
She turned. She arranged herself. She sat, very straight, in a throne that could have seated three of her, her sabatons swinging clear of the floor.
Then she gripped the armrests and lifted her chin high, with all the majesty available to somebody holding her crown out of her eyes through willpower alone.
Theater ran in that family, whatever else did. The hall went acutely, perfectly silent.
"Hear the crown," said Queen Felicity Valorian.
Six hundred nobles held their breath. The first decree of a reign was history, always. Chroniclers three kingdoms away would copy this sentence for centuries.
The queen of Vraven raised one gauntleted finger and pointed it at the old man standing beside the throne.

"Alexios Valorian." Her voice rang clear off the far doors. "For three whole years you schemed, and lied, and cheated, and tricked basically everybody, all so that you would never, ever have to leave me alone."
Her voice wobbled, and she stomped it flat, and kept going.

"So. By royal decree, the first of my reign: you are forbidden, from this day until the end of time, from calling yourself a terrible father. It is now illegal. I'll toss you in jail if you ever dare to utter that word ever again on yourself."
She sniffed, regally.
"As your queen, I demand it. As your daughter... I command it."
The great hall of Vraven stood in profound, scandalized, melting silence.

Somewhere in the middle rows, a hardened old countess pressed a handkerchief to her eyes with both hands. The Mediator, tucked discreetly near a pillar while sweating his balls off, wondered how he found himself inside the royal throne room. He beamed into his beard.

Alexios Valorian stood beside the throne he had held for long centuries and looked up at the young queen occupying it. For a moment the whole hall could see every one of those years on him, and none of them weighed anything at all.
Then the old king bowed his head to his daughter.
"...Yes, Your Majesty."
"Hmph." The queen crossed her arms, scarlet-eared. "Good."
The hall did not know whether to cheer or weep, and audibly attempted both.

And then, while the sound was still finding its shape, the queen of Vraven turned her head, and her gaze went across the great hall, past the peers, past the banners, to the man standing beside a red-eyed woman at the center of the floor.
The noise died on its own.
Felicity smirked.
Then the queen of Vraven rose from her throne, and walked.
One step.
Two steps.

Down the dais she came, holding her crown steady with one hand, every trace of the flustered girl folded away, and the hall parted in front of her. Nobles dropped as she passed, rank after rank, velvet going down like wheat.
"Quinlan." Her voice was clear and young, and it reached every corner of the seat of the nation. "My first decree had to be spent on disciplining my unruly father."
She crossed the last of the floor and stopped in front of the Primordial Villain, looking up.
Queen Felicity Valorian, sovereign of Vraven, lifted the great crown from her head, held it out before her in both gauntlets, and knelt.
"But my first act as queen of Vraven... is to ask for vassalage."

chapters.title: Chapter 1894 The Queen's Unexpected Offer
paragraphs: Queen Felicity Valorian knelt at the center of the great hall of Vraven with her crown held out in both gauntlets, and her question hung in the silence of six hundred held breaths.
Vassalage.
The word had finished echoing off the far doors, and nobody in the seat of the nation had remembered how to breathe since.
The chroniclers had stopped writing altogether.
The Primordial Villain looked down at the fourteen-year-old sovereign offering him her entire kingdom as soon as she was given the power to.
Then he reached down, wrapped her offered gauntlets in one big hand, and drew the queen of Vraven back up onto her feet, the crown still held between them.
Felicity blinked up at him, and for one second the queen of Vraven was entirely fourteen, glowing. "...Hehe."
Then she stepped back, and her voice rang clear off the marble.
"Before you answer, there is something I have to do first."
She settled the great crown onto her own head and turned her back on the most dangerous man alive to face her peerage.
'Oh?' Quinlan's brow climbed, and he gave the stage away without a word, because villains understood theater.
"Hear the crown," said the queen of Vraven.
The hall flinched. Her first decree had made a hardened countess weep into her handkerchief. Nothing in the young queen's face promised the second would be as gentle.
"House Silverwind." Her voice reached the last banner. "House Greenvale. House Duskmere. House Thornhollow. Step forward."
Movement rippled through the packed velvet.

Kaede Fujimori detached from the back rows in Silverwind's colors, Elder Chizuru a half-step behind her. Duke Alastair of Greenvale came grey and quiet, his twin daughters on his arms. Duke Zaren of Duskmere arrived white-haired and pleasant with Calienne on his arm, looking mildly delighted to be included in anything.
Duke Harland of Thornhollow came last, grizzled and heavy, lord of the realm's orchards and its moonwine. He wanted to be anywhere else on the continent.
Four houses stood before their queen.
The fifth name went unspoken, and every soul in the hall heard it anyway.
Felicity looked at the four of them for a long moment, and when she spoke again, the royal formula was gone. What was left was fourteen years old and completely serious.

"Long ago, my ancestors conquered your kingdoms." She said it plainly, a child reciting the family sin. "They took your crowns, wrote the Law of Accord, and named you stewards of the lands your houses had ruled as kings."
She let one breath pass.
"And every duke since has hated it."
"She cannot just say that..." an old count whispered somewhere in the middle rows, scandalized to his bones. Then he realized the only realistic explanation for all this. "Wait, am I dreaming?"

"Generations of endless plotting, and she just... gives it?!"

At the adventurers' table, Lilith stopped mid-bite. "...Holy shit," said the captain of the Scarlet Lilies, apple forgotten in her hand. "My niece might be crazier than her mom."

<Kneel.>
Duke Alastair of Greenvale stepped forward and knelt to his queen.
He went down smoothly, immediately, before the offer's echo had left the rafters, his twin daughters sinking in unison beside him.

The hall gasped as one chest.
"Greenvale?!" a baron blurted, court manners abandoned. "Greenvale declined?!"
"He fought the Accord his whole life...!"
"If any house walks free tonight, it should have been..."

Duke Harland of Thornhollow stared at his closest ally's bent back with his mouth open. Whatever he had braced himself for tonight, watching Alastair of Greenvale kneel like a man setting down a heavy crate had no place on the list.
'That fast, Alastair?' he thought. 'You didn't even make them wait for the echo.'
"House Silverwind," Felicity said.
Kaede Fujimori crossed the hall.
*Clack.* *Clack.*

Her heels were the only sound in the seat of the nation. The woman who had once held that duchy's seat in her own name stopped before the queen and knelt to her with a perfectly straight back, Elder Chizuru bowing low at her side.
"Silverwind made its choice, Your Majesty," Kaede said. "We stay."
Short, composed, finished. Chizuru's complaint-brush hung motionless over its scroll for the second time in recorded history.
"House Duskmere."
Duke Zaren of Duskmere blinked.
The white-haired duke looked at the queen, then at the enormous hall, then, with honest confusion, at his wife.
"I mean, why not?" he asked her, forgetting entirely to whisper. "Would you like to be queen?"
Calienne Valorian smiled at her husband with immense sweetness, and her elbow found his ribs, pointedly.
"Kneel, dear."

chapters.title: Chapter 1895 Submission or Independence
paragraphs: "Kneel, dear."
"Ah. Yes. Obviously." Duke Zaren of Duskmere knelt to his queen with visible relief, beaming up at her. "Duskmere declines, Your Majesty. Wholeheartedly."
Calienne sank down beside him toward her baby sister in a reverence of flawless elegance, and only her father, watching from the dais, caught the grin she aimed at the marble on the way down.
And then one duke remained.

Duke Harland of Thornhollow stood alone in the middle of the great hall of Vraven, every eye in the kingdom on his weathered face. The one thing his house had wanted for its entire recorded history lay at his feet, free for the taking.
Thornhollow had been a kingdom once.
He could be a king.
"He's going to take it," somebody whispered in the middle rows. "Look at him. He's going to take it."
The word had weight on his tongue, actual weight, handed down with the deeds and the vault keys.
His eyes moved without his permission.

To the Villain's family first, draped along the royal marble and thoroughly entertained. The samurai, the serpent, and the red-eyed woman whose arm was still bent wrong from caving in the chest of a duke.
To the flagstones next, the unmarked ones where the burning seam had been, the only whole stones left in the hall.
House Ravenshade had been the mightiest thing in this kingdom that did not wear a crown, and the crown's new friends had dismantled it between breakfast and dinner.

And his Thornhollow fed people. That was the whole of its power. Orchards, granaries, moonwine, good roads. His soldiers guarded wagons. A pale shadow, the military men had always called the Sustaining Arm's forces, usually to his face.
A king, then. A king of orchards, standing alone outside all of this.

Outside the realm his harvests fed, outside the crown's roads and the crown's protection, outside whatever came next. And anyone with working eyes could see the Villain was not finished, that everything he had touched so far had ended in a kneel.
And Alastair.
Harland had once pledged Alastair his full support with nothing but a nod. Together, they would become independent one day. Such was their promise.
Tonight the same man had gone down before the offer finished echoing.
'What did you see?' he thought, staring at the kneeling grey duke. 'What do you all see that I don't?'
But that was the lie, and he was too old to tell it to himself.
He saw it too. Everyone in this hall had seen it today, framed in ember light, screaming.
Duke Harland of Thornhollow closed his eyes, and let go of the dream his house had carried.
When he came forward, his steps were even. When he spoke, his voice was not.
"Your Majesty." He stopped. Started again. "My house... for my whole life, my house has wanted nothing in this world so much as the offer you just made."
Felicity looked up at the grizzled duke and waited.
"And I find..." His eyes went to the sealed flagstones, where Iris's hell had closed its gates. "...I find that the world in which we wanted it is gone. It went into that floor."
Duke Harland of Thornhollow knelt to Queen Felicity Valorian in the middle of the great hall.
"Thornhollow declines," he said, down at the marble.
The exhale that moved through the hall carried six hundred held breaths out with it.
Alexios Valorian watched from the dais and gave the hall nothing at all.
He had spent his entire reign scheming to rein in the rebelious dukes. His daughter had placed the finishing touches on his life's work.
The old king's eyes had an unnatural sheen to them.
Queen Felicity Valorian stood before four kneeling ducal houses and let the moment breathe.
Then she turned back around to face the Primordial Villain, reached up, and took the crown of Vraven off her head for the second time that day.
"Now it's whole." Her voice was clear and young, and it did not shake at all. "Every ducal house in Vraven was given the choice tonight, in front of everyone."
She held the crown out to Quinlan Elysiar in both gauntlets, and this time she stayed on her feet.
"So I will say it again. Vraven asks for vassalage."
The nobles watched the crown of the realm being held out to the most feared man alive, and this time nobody had any doubts left to hide behind.
Quinlan looked down at her.
'Fourteen years old,' he mused. 'What an amazing little lady you've become, Felicity.'
The Primordial Villain crossed the last of the distance and took the crown out of her gauntlets. He gave it one slow, appraising turn.
'It feels far heavier than it actually is,' he chuckled inwardly, weighing the invisible half of it in his hand.

He had dodged this exact fate once already, in a palace of living wood, by handing a freshly founded holy nation to two capable women and making a strategic retreat before any work could find his lap.
Overlord suited him far better than king. Kingdoms run by people he trusted, prospering in his name, while he handled the one job nobody else alive could do.
Becoming a supreme, undeniable existence.
In a harsh world like Thalorind, good governance was only half of the job. The other half was being powerful enough that no enemy could come and take what was yours.
Quinlan specialized in that area, and intended to keep things that way.
Thankfully, this realm already had its ruler.
A good girl who had already etched her name into the hearts of Vraven.
With his Tyrant of Commerce at her side, this little queen would run the human kingdom better than any villain with a saber ever could, and the two of them would enjoy every minute of it.

And the old bastard on the dais was not going anywhere. Alexios had no intention of dying anytime soon, and nobody knew this kingdom's machinery better than the man who had spent his reign running it. Felicity would be getting an advisor whether she wanted one or not.
He set the crown back on her head.
It slid straight down to her eyebrows.
"Keep it. It fits you better."
Then the same hand came down, petting the queen of Vraven's hair in front of her entire assembled peerage.

"Ehehe~" The giggle escaped before Felicity could stop it, and she stood there under his palm on her nation's most historic night, happy from crown to sabatons. <Lazy!!> she laughed into his mind, which was promptly ignored.

The grin came down at her, warm and villainous in equal measure. "I accept your vassalage, Queen of Vraven. You keep the crown and rule your people. But from today onwards, the kingdom, and everyone in it, is mine to look after."
He said the next part to the entire hall.
"And I take care of what's mine."
Far away in Elysaria, an entire nation would have cheered the sentence. Vraven's peerage did what humans do before a power they have finally stopped pretending to measure.

The four ducal houses bowed where they knelt, to the Villain now. Behind them the peers of the realm went down rank upon rank, velvet folding to the marble in a slow tide, to Quinlan Elysiar, liege lord of Vraven.
In the eastern gallery, Prince Elias lowered his head to the overlord his queen had chosen, and found the second submission of the day easier than the first.
Arch Priestess Elisabeth inclined her head to the man her doctrine had no chapter for.
Stormlord knelt to the Villain because the crown he served had spoken, gauntlet flat on the marble, iron all the way through.
Near his own pillar, the Mediator had gone very still, hands folded deep in his sleeves, watching hereditary sovereignty kneel on open marble, and keeping whatever he understood behind his beard.
Felicity beamed up at Quinlan from under the crown's rim, scarlet-eared and radiant. "Hehe!"
And into the girlish giggle of a monarch, a window unfolded across Quinlan's vision, a pane of quiet script hanging between him and six hundred bowed heads.
[The human people of Iskaris have acknowledged your dominion.]
[Peoples of Iskaris conquered: 2/4]
[Conquer the dwarven people and the beastkin people to claim rulership of Iskaris.]
[Reward: ???]
Quinlan read it once, unhurried.
'Already halfway,' he mused. 'And I didn't even have to draw the saber for this one.'
He flicked the window shut over the bowed heads of the human race and swept his gaze across the seat of the nation. The grin that arrived was slow, villainous, and thoroughly content.
"Let's get to work, shall we?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1896 Chatting Ladies
paragraphs: Serika Vael sat on the highest parapet of the royal palace of Vraven with one boot swinging over a hundred-meter drop, watching human nobility try to remember how to walk.
The trial was over. So were the coronation and the vassalage. The seat of the nation had finally begun spitting its peerage out into the night, and the show below was tremendous.

Their man had gone the other way, deeper into the palace, toward a private study with the old king and a river of clerks. The girls had taken one look at that particular door and reached a unanimous verdict.
"Let's spend some quality time together, shall we?" Serika had asked, and led the retreat. Many followed, knowing they'd just crowd the small room.
Now five of the most dangerous women alive lounged along the royal roofline with a liberated bottle of Thornhollow moonwine, and nobody below had any idea the new liege lord's family was rating them.
"Look at that one," Kitsara purred, pointing with a tail.
An elderly baron was being poured into his carriage by two footmen. His legs had given up somewhere around the second decree of the evening and never reported back for duty.
"That's the eighth one," the foxy declared with deep satisfaction.
"Seventh," Aurora corrected from her spot against a chimney, a plundered feast tray balanced on her knees. "The count by the fountain walked the last three steps on his own."
"He fell into the carriage."
"Falling forward counts."
"No, it doesn't."
"Okay, seven and a half."
"Deal."
The Slutty Foxy and nerdy alchemist reached a compromise.

Down in the torchlight, Blossom was helpfully carrying a limp countess to her coach under one arm, tail wagging, radiating civic virtue. She decided she'd increase her beloved Master's reputation among his harshest critics by being the most lovable ball of fluff to have ever existed.
"Look at her go," Lucille cooed. "Truly the best girl."
"Hehe~" Kitsara giggled. "If she hears that, she'll combust on the spot."
"...Best girl," Vex repeated, flat.
"Jealous?" Aurora grinned. "You could compete, you know. Go down, help a few nobles into their carriages just so they think better of Quinlan. Prime best-girl behavior."
Vex raised both hands and crossed her index fingers into a firm X.
"Never."
"Not even for the best girl standings?"
"I'd sooner help these sons of bitches into their graves. Iris and hubby will cull half of them soon enough anyhow. Waste of effort. Hmph."
"Heh," Aurora chuckled and left it at that.

"You all are having too much fun ridiculing these losers," Aurora said, and ate another tart.
Lucille took the bottle on its next orbit and looked down at the emptying court, at banners she used to cross streets to avoid.
"Can you blame them? These houses have been hunting us for some time. Especially poor Vexie."
"You seem awfully happy, Miss Harem Head," Serika smiled, though she already knew the answer.
"Tonight my father knelt because I told him to." Lucille grinned down at the courtyard, warm all the way through. "The wine helps too~"
"To the misery of every bastard who ever chased us." Serika reclaimed the bottle and raised it at Lucille before drinking.
"Does Quinlan count?" Kitsara asked. "He's been chasing our booty for a long time..."
"..." Silence and wry expressions welcomed her words.
Seeing her joke didn't manage to land, she took the drink from Serika's hand. "Stop looking at me like that! It was funny."
Her eyes drooped as she lifted her head back and began chugging. "Let me drink my sorrow away..."
The bottle went around again. The courtyard kept emptying. Somewhere below, a herald was still calling houses in a voice that had gone hoarse before sunset.
"Actually, yeah," Vex spoke up with an extremely sly tone. "He's been chasing our booty for quite some time. Mine the longest..."

"..." It was her turn to get wry gazes aimed at her person. But unlike the foxy, she grinned through it all. "But can you say the same, Kitsara? You jumped into his lap on day one, there was no chasing of any kind for your fluffy behind..."
"Grr!!" Kitsara growled, all five tails standing on end. Then they lost their will to fight. "Give me more booze."
"Stop bullying her into alcoholism..." Lucille muttered, reaching over to hold the dejected foxkin girl to her bosom. "It's okay sweetie. Quinlan likes your booty just as much as everyone else's..."
"Mommy..." Kitsara nestled her head further into Lucille's hold. "If only your breasts were bigger..."
"..." The Bloodmonger's forehead suddenly began featuring a throbbing vein.
"You know what the best part is?" Aurora stretched out across the stone. "A week ago, this kingdom had paper on us all. Bounty notices. Official ones, with the ugly woodcut Quin had."
"The woodcut was sheer slander I still haven't forgiven that grumpy old man for," Vex agreed. "Hubby is far more handsome."
"And now we all but own the presses that printed them," Aurora went on, savoring every word, "and the walls they were nailed to. I say we frame one."
"He would hang it over the throne," Lucille said.
"He absolutely would," Aurora said. "That's the problem."
Serika leaned back on her palms and looked across the palace beneath them, the torchlit courts, the banners, the whole velvet nation their man had accepted with a head pat.
"I abdicated a throne to chase that scoundrel," she mused, full of fond remembrance. "Signed the oath, handed him my Shard, and walked out of Vulkaris with one bag."
"And?" Lucille prompted, grinning.

"And tonight I watched a young miss I adore so much hand him an entire kingdom." Serika shook her head slowly. "I taught that man his first proper stance. Somewhere along the way, the student got greedy."
"You conquer by punching. He conquers by headpats." Kitsara nodded sagely into Lucille's breasts. "Frankly, I prefer his method. It transfers to the bedroom a lot better."
"Ask Ayame which she prefers~" Aurora mused.
"...Let's not go there," Kitsara shook her head. "You call me slutty, but Miss Second in Command? Now that's a proper depraved woman I say."
"Hey now..." Lucille spoke up, gently, motherly. "Ayame might enjoy a bit of choking and other questionable acts, but even she doesn't like being punched."
"Yeah, aside from getting her butt slapped like there's no tomorrow," Serika snorted, finding that girl's interests quite amusing to say the least.
"... That's slapping, to be fair," Vex decided to join Ayame's defense case. Then, with blushing cheeks, she added, "I myself won't say no to-"
"Okay, okay. Let's return to the topic at hand, enough about butts being destroyed," Aurora sighed.
The topic quickly wound down after that. Below them, the last carriages were forming a line at the gates, lamps swaying.
"Iris cried in front of the entire peerage," Lucille said, softer, to nobody in particular.
Nobody needed the name.
"She did," Serika nodded.
"Is she going to be alright?" Aurora asked. A straight question, no garnish.
Serika gave it the honest thought it deserved.

"Not all the way, I'm afraid," she exhaled slowly. "What was done to her doesn't finish healing, probably ever. Childhood trauma like that is more or less impossible to fully overcome, for she doesn't have a baseline to return to after having healed. It just stops being the whole of her, that's all. What I hope for is that she builds a bigger life around the wound until it's one room in a large house, instead of being the house."
"She has the biggest life on the continent to build with," Lucille said. "A creed, a road, that ridiculous title he gave her."
"Partner in crime," Vex mused, from inside her own smile. "She fought a level seventy-four with a broken arm for it."
"And what a fight that was!" Serika flexed her muscles on reflex. "She made me far too proud."
"And did you see her face in the pile?" Kitsara giggled. "Under all the swearing? Radiant. She was so beautiful..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1897 Council of Hags
paragraphs: "Radiant and educational with all the swear words she introduced to our posh audience," Aurora chuckled.
"Nobody ever tells her we saw the tears, okay?" Serika asked. "Or the brilliant smile for that matter."
"Obviously," said everyone else.
"And the cutest queen of them all." Lucille pressed a hand over her heart. "Fourteen. She shooed the king off his own throne. 'Up, up!' With both gauntlets!"
"I nearly bit through my own tail trying not to break into howling laughter at that," Kitsara admitted. "It would've ruined the moment."

"She offered four dukes their freedom to make the kneeling real, in front of six hundred witnesses, on her first night under the crown." Serika whistled low. "As an ex-ruler, her guts simply floored me. Who would've thought that I'd end up having a fourteen-year-old role model?"
"Well, your husband is like eleven months old, so it kind of fits..." Lucille shrugged, full of playfulness.
"..." Serika's eyes narrowed. "You're one to talk. Your daughter is what, twenty times older than your husband?"
"D-don't put it like that!" Lucille yelped suddenly.
"Can we agree, for all our sakes, to never bring up Quin's biological age again?" Aurora begged.
"Hehe! I don't mind. It's not shameful," Kitsara snickered into Lucille's breasts.
"Same. Hubby is hubby, no matter how old or in what physical form..." Vex muttered with eyes that would've alarmed any sane person. Her four friends, however, were fully used to her manic expression.
A second bottle had appeared from somewhere, already half gone.
"Look at us." Kitsara sighed happily, moving the topic along. "Runaways, criminals, exiles, and two grannies, lounging on the roof of the world."
"Excuse me." Vex's eyes moved with dangerous precision. "Grannies?"
"Elders! Respected, beautiful elders."
"You're fifty, foxy."
"And in fifty years I'll join the council of wrinkly hags with grace, unlike some people."
"A hundred doesn't qualify you to join the council," Serika scoffed. "That's too young."
"Khm! Damned gatekeeping hag! Khm!" Kitsara coughed into Lucille's bosom.
Serika elected to wrap her fist around five lush tails.
"H-hey! Don't you dare-" Kitsara yelped immediately.
Serika didn't pull. "That's right. Be a good girl and respect your elders."
"Ugh! Blackmailing hag- I mean nice and beautiful tanned lady!"

"...Good," Serika smirked. Then she turned her head to her dejected friend in the wrinkly hags council. "Cheer up, Vexie. Between us? I don't think we'll be the eldest ladies around here for much longer."
Vex opened her mouth for the obvious question.
Nothing came out.
The rooftop had gone conspicuously quiet. Lucille smiled at the horizon and said nothing at all. Aurora studied her tart.
The question answered itself before the Hexwitch finished asking it.

She remembered the glimpse of violet glow above her master's womb. She remembered the rescue nobody would explain, one heated far past all sense. The same flat voice had filed the whole matter away back then: it did not concern her.
Warmth arrived, sudden and fierce, all of it for her master.
One of Vex's hands drifted, without asking her permission first, to rest low on her own belly, over the mark that made her his.

Her master had pulled a starving orphan out of a lionkin-ravaged village, handed her a knife and a forest, and built her into the woman who seduced the greatest man to have ever existed, one merciless lesson at a time.
In all the years since, as far as Vex had ever been allowed to see, Black Fang had kept nothing warm for herself.
"Good," she whispered, slowly, fondly. Her thumb moved once over the fabric above the mark. "She deserves it... She deserves all the happiness in the world..."
Nobody asked who. Nobody teased her. Lucille reached over and squeezed Vex's ankle once, and the rooftop let her be.
The peace lasted right up until Aurora frowned.
"Wait," said the group's foremost scientific mind, tart halfway to her mouth. "Are you two actually sure you're the eldest in the harem?"
"You keep saying it like a confirmed measurement. Who confirmed it?" Aurora set the tray down, professionally troubled now. "What about Kaelira?"
The name landed on the rooftop and sat there.
"What about Kaelira?" Vex asked, with the first stirrings of a growl.

"She's an elf. Elves live long and consider the subject rude. We all treat her like the shy little tomboy sister of the group." Aurora looked around the circle. "Has she ever actually told anyone her age? A number? Ever?"
The girls thought about it.
The girls kept thinking about it.
"I've been talking down to her for months," Kitsara said, stricken. "She let me."
"She lets everyone," Lucille murmured, awed. "She blushes, says nothing, and lets us all assume."
Vex was already reaching for the family link.
<Kaelira.>
The link took its time answering, which was unusual for the most dutiful member of the family.
<...Yes?> came the smith's voice, wary from the first syllable.
<How old are you?>
Silence.
<I... um.> The pause stretched for entire seconds. <I don't... know?>
Five women who had all watched Kaelira measure a hair's width of steel by eye recognized the dodge before it finished crossing the link.
"She's lying~" Kitsara sang.
<Kaelira,> Vex growled down the link. <How. Old. Are. You.>
The next pause was the longest one yet. Serika used it to take a satisfied pull off the bottle.
<Umm...> The shy voice climbed half an octave, aiming for casual and missing by a league. <Maybe a... little older than you thought...?>
<Older by how much?!>
The link went quiet on the smith's end, with great politeness.
<Kaelira. KAELIRA!!!>
Nothing came back. The forge was closed for the night.
Vex stared straight up at the stars.
"She hung up," she announced to the rooftop, flatly. "She hung up on me."
The rooftop broke.
Serika howled. Lucille laughed herself sideways into Aurora, who was wheezing something about sample sizes. Kitsara simply fell over.
"This shameless bitch!" Vex was upright now, gesturing at the uncaring sky. "She let me wail in my inferiority all this time while being the actual oldest harem member?!"
Serika recovered her breathing first, reached over, and thumped Vex on the back.
"Hey. Hey. It doesn't count."
"It counts!" Vex hissed. "It absolutely does count!"

"She's an elf. Elf years are a different coin entirely." Serika waved a generous hand. "Even if she's five hundred, in human years that's... what, fifty? You'd still be the older woman. By quite a bit, actually."
Vex's head rotated toward her, slowly, joint by joint. Her eyes were two red pentagrams of murder.
"What did you just say to me?"
"That we're still the grannies of the gang for all intents and purposes."
"No! I refuse!" Vex flopped back down onto the ledge with a huff they probably heard at the gates.
After a moment, her hand found its way back to the warm spot low on her belly, and stayed. "I hate you all so much... Messing with this old lady's feelings... At least hubby would never..."
"Hehe!" the girls giggled together.
Below them, the last carriage rolled out through the palace gates. Blossom waved after it from the gatehouse.
It was time to finalize the details of the handover to the budding empire in the making.

chapters.title: Chapter 1898 Final Item
paragraphs: Quinlan Elysiar, liege lord of Vraven for all of twenty minutes, had already found the best chair in the royal study and claimed it.
The study belonged to Alexios. The desk had passed to new management that afternoon.
Queen Felicity Valorian sat behind it, crown riding just above her eyebrows, and read every line of every decree before allowing it anywhere near her inkwell.
Her father stood at her shoulder with his sleeves rolled, demoted from king to royal advisor before dinner and wearing it well.
"This one still cites the toll schedule we tore up." Felicity tapped the offending page. "Why is it in my pile?"
"Because its author hoped Your Majesty would not read it," said Alexios.
"Hmph." She struck the clause and initialed the margin, hard.
The budding empire's half of the paperwork was proceeding differently.
"Sign here," said Jasmine.
Quinlan signed.
"And here. Initials at the bottom. Neatly, please, my love."
Quinlan signed with excellent penmanship. Well, as excellent as he could muster.

The Tyrant of Commerce had entered the room with an abacus in one hand and the big ledger under her arm, taken one look at her man alone in a room with unattended state documents, and requisitioned the entire pile.
Every page reached Quinlan already folded open to the right line. By the third decree, she had started praising his signature.
"Lovely~ And this one."
Ayame had taken the window seat sideways, chin on her knee, watching her lover, the man taking over the entire Iskaris continent in real time, be directed like a boy guided by his mother.
The petite samurai was having the time of her life watching the scene.
"You didn't read that one," she observed as Quinlan signed something.
"Of course not. Jasmine read it."
"That's not how ruling works, Quin."
He merely shrugged and kept going, signing where Jasmine pointed.
A snort escaped the samurai.
Across the room, the fourteen-year-old was interrogating her third clause of the hour. But over here, the most feared man alive signed wherever a warm finger tapped.
Ayame filed the comparison away, deeply fond, and kept it to herself.
"Keep signing, my mighty conqueror~"
Mostly kept it to herself.
The boring stretch had gone quickly, all things considered.
Ravenshade's lands would sit under crown administrators until the audit finished combing them.

The duchy's armies were already marching under Stormlord's marshals. The audit itself had taken one second to assign: it stayed with Iris, all of it, as deep as she cared to dig, for as long as she cared to keep digging.
The auditor in question had been confiscated by Seraphiel the moment the hall emptied, broken arm and all.
That was where they learned what else the new class had brought with it.
Seraphiel laid healing light on the arm. The break stayed exactly where it was, and Iris went grey to the lips, swayed once, and had to be caught before she hit the floor.
They tried twice more, gently. She came closer to going under each time.
The Demon of Vengeance could not be healed.
Seraphiel had gone very quiet at that, then steered her friend out by the good shoulder with the look she usually saved for a locked door.
"I have ideas about your class," she had said brightly.
Iris had gone. She had also told the entire corridor exactly where the elf could put her ideas.
Felicity had lasted admirably deep into the agenda before her first nod.
"Brain hurts..." she muttered weakly.

On the second, her chin hit her breastplate mid-sentence and the crown slid down to her nose. Feng Jiai appeared at the door on pure best-friend instinct, hauled her queen up onto her back, and carried her off to bed.
Alexios claimed the emptied desk without ceremony, rolled his sleeves a turn higher, and went to work on the wreckage of the day one document at a time. A stamp rose and fell under his hand.
Despite stepping down, he retained every right needed to govern the lands. But now, Felicity could dismiss him on a whim.
They kept going until both sides were done with their respective paperwork.
That left the last item.
"Item the final," read the young clerk who had drawn the short straw, and his voice thinned as he arrived at it. "Of the dissolved estate of House Ravenshade... there remains... one... issue."
He looked at the fireplace, went pale, and stopped reading.
Morgana Ravenshade had been standing beside that fireplace for the better part of an hour.
She had arrived under a crown writ delivered by a page who would not meet her eyes, and she had assumed, on entering, that her disposition would be the evening's first order of business.
She had then watched grain schedules, toll ledgers, and a dispute over stable fees each receive the full and serious attention of the room.
Her left eye had developed a twitch somewhere around the stable fees.
"Ah," Quinlan said at last, brightening. "The greatest wife of all time. How could I possibly forget?"
Morgana's mana came up hard enough to stir the ash in the grate.
The Primordial Villain spread both hands toward the woman by the fireplace.
"Old friend. The new era deserves a gift between our houses, and I've decided on it. Your wife. Returned to you, whole and intact."
Morgana's whole seething stance came undone at once.
Freedom? Just like that?!
"Alexios-"
The stamp came down on the next document.
"The estate of Ravenshade is under audit seal," interjected Alexios. "Nothing leaves it until Iris Ravenclaw signs off on every last asset."

"Asset?!" The word came off the fireplace at a pitch that made the poker ring in its stand. "I am not estate property, you desiccated old vulture! All these years of marriage, and you cannot even look up from your papers!"

"You are a slave, an asset. Whether the legality of your enslavement holds is a matter to be settled in court, or by Her Majesty's decree," grumbled Alexios, not looking up from his papers. "I no longer have the power to make such decisions."
"Hah?!"
"You wound me, old friend." Quinlan pressed a hand to his chest. "She's a queen. The second strongest elemental mage on the continent. A national treasure."
"Slavery outranks a marriage," Alexios said, initialing a margin.
Quinlan grinned into it. He was more amused by this old bastard's attitude than ever before.
"The marriage came first. Older claims win."
"You can't even read a legal document, so why are you parroting claims that make no sense? Ask your wife to educate you on the matter before you speak up, please."
The stamp came down again.
Despite having just been verbally insulted, Quinlan only grew more amused. 'I see how it is, you damned old bastard...' he chuckled inwardly.
Ayame had given up all pretense of minding the window. She leaned forward over her knee, following the volley with open delight.
"Stop this!" Morgana howled.
"In a moment," Quinlan told her pleasantly, and returned to the negotiation. "The northern keeps, Alexios. I'll add both of them to the deal."
"You're paying to get rid of your strongest slave?!" Morgana stomped her feet.
"I have keeps."
"The granary at Silver Hollow, then. Fully stocked, freshly audited."
"Half stocked," said Jasmine, without looking up from the ledger.
"Half stocked, freshly audited."
"You are offering me my own confiscations."
"With incredible generosity."

"Armies redraw their maps when I am rumored to be in the area!" Morgana's voice climbed with every word, mana grinding in her veins. "Entire clans faint at my name! And you're trying to pay a man to cart me away!"
"Yes..." Quinlan nodded along, delighted, as though she were making his pitch for him.
Then Quinlan added, "You're strong, no doubt. But..." he shrugged. "Eh."
"Eh?! What do you mean eh?!"
"Where's your devotion, old friend?" Quinlan tried next. "She gave you your heirs."
"A fact I intend to honor from a distance," said Alexios.
The fireplace tools had begun to rattle.
"You preening, self-satisfied pair of disgusting, creep-"
Both men turned to look at her with identical mild interest, waiting for the rest.
The rest did not come. Morgana's mouth closed. Her left eye twitched, once.
"See that?" Quinlan opened a palm toward her, for Alexios. "She even learned how to behave while serving as my slave. She's not the same terrible wife you remember."
"The gravity of the improvement stifles me."

chapters.title: Chapter 1899 Humiliating a Haughty Cunt
paragraphs: "The gravity of the improvement stifles me."
"...Well, she's on the right path."
"The temper is in her veins," Alexios said. "Ask her brother or sister."
Somewhere in another world entirely, her brother declined to comment. Lilith, meanwhile, sneezed.
"Don't look so betrayed, rabid dog," Quinlan told her, warm as anything. "This is generosity. I'm playing marriage counselor for two people who wanted to kill me not long ago."
"I still want to kill you!" Morgana clarified with a guttural shout. Then, for good measure, she added, "And I do not want to be reunited with this wrinkly piece of shit!"
Quinlan leaned back in his stolen chair and considered the deadlock.
Words had failed. Bribery had failed. Devotion had failed.
Time for art.
A pinch of mortar peeled off the fireplace masonry, crossed the study in a lazy spiral, and settled on the desk between the two men, where it became a pair of small clay figures.
One wore a tiny crown. The other held a tiny staff.
And the two figures held each other's hands, like a perfect husband and wife.
"Look at them, old friend," Quinlan said warmly. "Isn't this what you want?"
Alexios set down the stamp and gave the sculpture his full administrative attention.
"He looks miserable."
"Come on. At your age, you need a nice, tender woman to take care of you..."
"You just made me stop aging. Stop treating me like a dying man."
"Damn. What a blunder," Quinlan scoffed.
"..." Alexios examined him for a long second with a perfect poker face. Then he sighed. "The likeness isn't there."
"Hmm..." Quinlan merely glanced at the sculpture, and the staff-bearer gained a scowl and a twitching left eye. "Better?"
"Now it's accurate." The stamp resumed.

"It could be like this every evening." Quinlan made the little couple wave at the former king. "Tea. Companionship. She might be the continent's biggest bitch, but she's still the mother of your children."
"Some relationships just aren't meant to continue. And I take my tea alone, unless one of my children has time to spare."
"Hm." Quinlan looked down at his figurines with great disappointment, then back up. "Are you sure?"
"Yes-"
The male figure bent the female figure over and positioned himself behind her.
Then...
*Slam!*
Clay began slapping against clay on the royal desk in a smooth, practiced rhythm.
The young clerk set down the agenda, bowed to no one in particular, and evacuated the study at a dignified sprint.
"Quinlan Elysiar!" Jasmine was on her feet with the big ledger raised overhead. "We are in the royal palace! Put those away this instant!"
At the window, Ayame made a sound like a punctured bellows and pitched sideways, catching the frame at the last instant with one flailing hand.
"You... you depraved, shameless...!" Morgana had gone scarlet from collar to hairline. "Destroy them! Destroy them at once!"
Alexios looked at the tiny figures fucking on the desk in front of him.
He kept looking at them.
Jasmine scolded, Ayame wheezed, Morgana shrieked, and the former king of Vraven studied the performance through all of it with wry, unhurried interest.
"Her form was never that enthusiastic," he finally said.
Morgana's scream cracked one of the study's windows.
Her staff was in her hand before she finished deciding to draw it.
She braced for the leash.

The subjugation ruled her absolutely. She could not raise a hand against her master. In a real battle she could not so much as jostle his spellwork; the bond would seize her mid-gesture and hold her like a doll until the danger passed.
The bond did not stir.

Her master lounged in his chair, entirely undefended, and the puppets fornicating on the desk registered to the almighty subjugation as exactly what they were to him. Toys. Nothing she did to them would count as an attack on anything.
She was not being permitted. She was beneath preventing.
"You insufferable...!" The Elemental Sovereign aimed her staff at two clay figurines and began to chant.
Runes wheeled around the staff's head in three rings, her voice shook the inkwells, and the strongest human mage on the continent brought her full ceremony down upon the royal desk.
"[Infernal Gale]!"
A lance of white fire needled across the study and struck the lovers at the exact moment of the downstroke. Clay detonated into powder.

The ash never reached the desk. Quinlan's mana flared around it, lazy and vast, and her own flames soaked into the powder mid-fall until it landed as two magma figures, cheerfully molten, the female riding the male at a triumphant angle, tiny arms thrown skyward in victory.
Quinlan had not looked away from Alexios. The magic happened around him anyway, obedient to nothing but intent.
"Are you sure sure?" he asked, smug in a way that deserved criminal charges.
The crimson swirl of Morgana's eyes spun into a blur. She chanted again, and a torrent of conjured water drowned the desk, quenching the couple in a shriek of steam.

The steam curled toward the glint in Quinlan's eyes, condensed, and became two translucent water figures, the female folded fully in half with her ankles hooked behind her own neck, bent in a way only a liquid could survive.
"Stop improving them!" The hearthstones had begun to crack beneath her boots.
Her next verse froze the desk solid. The ice pair simply continued, joints grinding on with tiny, dignified squeaks.
"Are you sure sure sure?" Quinlan asked, undisturbed.

She shattered them with a hammer of compressed air, and the sound that came with it was not a word. The shards whirled up into a wind pair, barely visible at all, their indecency carried entirely by motion, and imagination did far crueler work than clay ever had.

By then, Ayame had both sleeves stuffed against her mouth, shaking hard enough to creak the window frame. Jasmine had stopped scolding by the time the ice arrived, and the big ledger now stood open in front of her face like a privacy screen.
They went through lightning at some point. Nobody in the room ever spoke of it again.

By the end of it, Morgana Ravenshade stood in a nimbus of unspent fury, hair drifting in a wind that did not exist, her staff smoking, five spells of continental grade wasted on pornographic figurines. Every flawless counterspell had supplied the material for the next act.
Quinlan sat unmoved, one hand draped over the armrest. His mana flared where it pleased, and the world rearranged itself to match his mood.

Five hundred years of study had gone into her mastery. He played seven elements like finger puppets, bored, zero-handed, to needle her husband. Watching him do it frayed the edges of her sanity. It always did.
"The desk was my great-grandfather's," Alexios noted into the quiet, initialing a margin that had survived. "This rabid female rode the poor male figure so hard the desk was damaged."
"I will burn this palace to the ground!"
At last the Primordial Villain leaned back and conceded the field.
"We're deadlocked, old friend."
"So we are."
"A matter this delicate shouldn't be rushed." His grin gained ceremony. "We'll sleep on it."
"Agreed." Alexios set the stamp down at last and folded his hands, matching him gravity for gravity. "A decision of this weight deserves rested minds. A week, at minimum."
"A month," Quinlan countered solemnly. "Statecraft."
"A season. There are precedents to consult."
"Years, if we must. The realm asks patience of us all."
Morgana Ravenshade stood beside the fireplace of a palace she was still formally banished from and understood, with perfect clarity, what had just been done to her.
It had never mattered which of them won. Both of them had been fighting to lose.
The strongest human mage alive, and the argument had been over who had to keep her.
Her husband had refused her without lifting his eyes from the paperwork. Her master had spent minutes desperately trying to give her away for free, throwing in granaries to sweeten the deal.
And now the two men had adjourned, cheerfully, on the question of who must suffer her, with every intention of extending the deliberations into the next century.
On tonight's agenda, she had ranked below the stable fees.
The stamp came down one final time.
"The item is tabled," said Alexios. "Session adjourned."
Morgana looked from one man to the other. Both had already returned to their papers.
The twitch had long since spread from her eye to her entire frame. A sound left her with no letters in it.
"May both of you scum die a dog's death," she snarled on her way to the door, robes snapping behind her. "ARGHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!!!"
The study door boomed shut behind her hard enough to wake clerks two corridors away.
The hallway outside stood dark and empty, the palace finally asleep around it.
Morgana made it two steps before she stopped.
Through the heavy door behind her, muffled, came the sound of both men snickering together.
She could just make out the words.
Something about the stable fees.
The Elemental Sovereign of Vraven stood alone in the dark of the palace her teenage daughter ruled, robes trembling at the hem, and began tearing up.
"What have I done to deserve this...?"

The fact that she treated her husband of nearly five centuries as absolute trash, and that she hunted her now-master with the intention of strapping him to a table and studying what's inside him, had not quite crossed her mind.
With the paperwork of Vraven done, Quinlan Elysiar owned half of Iskaris.
Now, it was time to see to the other half.

By the end of it, Morgana Ravenshade stood in a nimbus of unspent fury, hair drifting in a wind that did not exist, her staff smoking, five spells of continental grade wasted on pornographic figurines.
Every flawless counterspell had supplied the material for the next act.
Quinlan sat unmoved, one hand draped over the armrest.
His mana flared where it pleased, and the world rearranged itself to match his mood.
Five hundred years of study had gone into her mastery.
He played seven elements like finger puppets, bored, zero-handed, to needle her husband.
Watching him do it frayed the edges of her sanity.
It always did.
"The desk was my great-grandfather's," Alexios noted into the quiet, initialing a margin that had survived.
"This rabid female rode the poor male figure so hard the desk was damaged."
"I will burn this palace to the ground!"
At last the Primordial Villain leaned back and conceded the field.
"We're deadlocked, old friend."
"So we are."
"A matter this delicate shouldn't be rushed." His grin gained ceremony.
"We'll sleep on it."
"Agreed." Alexios set the stamp down at last and folded his hands, matching him gravity for gravity.
"A decision of this weight deserves rested minds.
A week, at minimum."
"A month," Quinlan countered solemnly.
"Statecraft."
"A season.
There are precedents to consult."
"Years, if we must.
The realm asks patience of us all."
Morgana Ravenshade stood beside the fireplace of a palace she was still formally banished from and understood, with perfect clarity, what had just been done to her.
It had never mattered which of them won.
Both of them had been fighting to lose.
The strongest human mage alive, and the argument had been over who had to keep her.
Her husband had refused her without lifting his eyes from the paperwork.
Her master had spent minutes desperately trying to give her away for free, throwing in granaries to sweeten the deal.
And now the two men had adjourned, cheerfully, on the question of who must suffer her, with every intention of extending the deliberations into the next century.
On tonight's agenda, she had ranked below the stable fees.
The stamp came down one final time.
"The item is tabled," said Alexios.
"Session adjourned."
Morgana looked from one man to the other.
Both had already returned to their papers.
The twitch had long since spread from her eye to her entire frame.
A sound left her with no letters in it.
"May both of you scum die a dog's death," she snarled on her way to the door, robes snapping behind her.
"ARGHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!!!"
The study door boomed shut behind her hard enough to wake clerks two corridors away.
The hallway outside stood dark and empty, the palace finally asleep around it.
Morgana made it two steps before she stopped.
Through the heavy door behind her, muffled, came the sound of both men snickering together.
She could just make out the words.
Something about the stable fees.
The Elemental Sovereign of Vraven stood alone in the dark of the palace her teenage daughter ruled, robes trembling at the hem, and began tearing up.
"What have I done to deserve this...?"

The fact that she treated her husband of nearly five centuries as absolute trash, and that she hunted her now-master with the intention of strapping him to a table and studying what's inside him, had not quite crossed her mind.
With the paperwork of Vraven done, Quinlan Elysiar owned half of Iskaris.
Now, it was time to see to the other half.

chapters.title: Chapter 1900 Rapid Development
paragraphs: The study door had barely stopped shuddering from Morgana's exit when Jasmine slid the next decree in front of Quinlan, folded open to the right line.
"Sign here, my love."
Quinlan signed.
"We're through the worst of it. Hang in there~" she purred, kissing his cheek lovingly.
The pile under her arm had stopped looking infinite somewhere around the stable fees; what remained was the stubborn tail of a kingdom changing hands.
Across the room, Alexios's stamp kept its even rhythm over the crown's half. Ayame had never left her window seat, chin back on her knee.
Halfway down the next page, a chime started up from inside his pocket ring. He fished out a fist-sized communication crystal, glanced at it, and answered without breaking his signature.
"Myra. Miss me already?"
"Miss you?!" The crystal crackled with the force of it. "Do you know what reached my desk tonight, you impossible man? Do you know what I have been listening to for the past hour?"
"Enlighten me."

"My royal guard!" A stomp came through the crystal, distant and unmistakable. "Elowen! The one I ordered to guard your family with her life! I gave her to you whole, Slaver Son. Armored. Sober. And tonight she calls me on a borrowed artifact, from a drinking hall, under the dwarven mountain, where you left her!"
Ayame sat up on the window seat. "The escort," she whispered, delighted. "The one who always hissed so much."
"I thought it'd serve her well to spend some time with the dwarves," Quinlan said into the crystal.
"She has been there for days!"
"Yes. And?"

A rustle came through the link, and then a second sound arrived, tinny and distant: Myrasyn holding her crystal against another one. Live from under a mountain, the royal study of Vraven received several seconds of an elven royal guard leading what sounded like an entire drinking hall through the chorus of a dwarven song.
"That," Myrasyn said, returning, "is what guards your family's honor tonight. But she did not call me to sing drunkenly all night, Quinlan."
Quinlan listened.
"The mountain's council has declared my people treacherous and every treaty between our races void. And you, they named enemy of the mountain. To be resisted and eliminated."
"Eliminated," Quinlan chuckled darkly, savoring it. "That's adorable."

"An hour after they posted it, the mountain rose. Smiths, commoners, soldiers, the whole under-tier. The First Hammer lit every forge in the royal smithy and declared open rebellion against her own lords."
The study had gone quiet, Jasmine's pen had stopped mid-line, and Ayame's chin had come off her knee entirely.
Quinlan leaned back in his stolen chair, and the grin that answered it was pure, warm villainy.
"Brokk made her choice quicker than I expected," he said fondly.
"What do you intend to do, Quinlan?" Myrasyn's voice pressed. "They're gearing for war."
"If it's war they want..." He set the pen down and stood. "Then war they get."
"Haha..." Myrasyn giggled under her breath. "I knew you'd say this. Do you need help? I can organize-"
"I'll not use the first deployment of my adorable elves on such a small matter," Quinlan declined with extreme nonchalance. On the other end of the line, the blonde woman's lips went from ear to ear.
'Here he is... The man I kneeled to.'
"I understand. Good luck."
Quinlan cracked his neck. "I'm afraid not even a Goddess of Luck can help those ignorant sons of bitches."
The crystal vanished back into his ring.

Jasmine was already pulling a ledger from the bottom of her stack, flipping pages with two fingers. "The joint reconstruction drafts are on the table," she murmured. "We need to rein the dwarves in so we can start delivering the terms promised to the Beastman Confederation."
In return for turning back after Elvardia's defeat, Quinlan and Myrasyn had promised war reparations for their people. But to actually deliver they needed dwarves doing construction work.
"On it," Quinlan grinned, visibly ready to shed dwarf blood.
"So." Jasmine set the ledger aside, gathered the unsigned remainder of his pile, and tapped it square against the desk. "Dwarf lands."
"Dwarf lands," Quinlan agreed.
And then he didn't move.
Jasmine looked at the most feared man alive standing in the middle of the royal study.
He looked back at her like a misbehaving puppy.
She smiled softly with the tired patience of a mother whose little ruffian had just begged her to be let out to play.
Jasmine sighed, long and deep, and the sigh ruffled the top of the decree pile.
"Fine." She waved the decree toward the door. "Go. I'll handle the rest of the pile and take care of things here."
He crossed the study in three steps, caught her by the waist, and lifted her clean off the floor.
"Quin...!"
The kiss was big, unhurried, and entirely indifferent to the state documents pinned under her elbow. Her toes left the ground, found nothing, and stopped looking.
When he finally let her breathe, he didn't set her down. He brought his lips to her ear instead.
"Brace yourself, you beyond amazing creature," he whispered. "I'll be imprinting that delicate belly of yours very soon."
"!!" Jasmine stopped working. All of her, at once.
Her eyes went wide, then bright gold, then wide and bright gold together, and the flush climbed from her collar to the roots of the working knot in one smooth pour.
The Bloodfather ritual...
"I... you..." The Tyrant of Commerce, negotiator of nations, stammered. "Quin! I don't have time to spend knocked out! The handover, the tax rolls, Greenvale's quarter-close...!"
"The girls all got through it quick," he whispered, supportive.
"The girls are strong." It came out small, with a little laugh that didn't fit her at all. "I'm..."
He kissed her again, mid-word.
Her protest died between his mouth and hers, and into the quiet where it had been, his voice arrived directly against her mind.
<No excuses, my love.>
She had deferred the mark once because of schedules and priorities until even she believed the costume.
Every woman in the family had let her keep it. He had let her keep it. The only woman in the house wearing no mark at all was the one who ran the house.
<We've stalled long enough. Both of us.>
Her breath stopped against him.
Then they closed, and she kissed him back, state documents and all, her fingers curling into his collar with none of the boardroom in them.
When they parted, she stayed in his arms a moment longer, forehead against his jaw, and the words came out in a murmur he felt more than heard.
"...Okay," she breathed. "Just... give me some time to prepare mentally. A little. That's all I ask."
"Just a little," Quinlan agreed, and set her down gently on her feet.
Jasmine straightened her blouse, retrieved her dignity from around her ankles, and reassembled the governor piece by piece in front of him. The blush stayed. It went magnificently with the gold.
"Out," she declared, snatching up a decree folder and shooing him with it. "Out! Some of us have a kingdom to transfer. And that kiss goes on your account, young man, don't think I wasn't counting!"
"Scary."
"Shoo, shoo!" she huffed, more adorable than ever before.
"Do try to leave the mountain standing," Alexios said to Quinlan, not looking up from the desk he had reclaimed. "It's very valuable."
"I know. I'll just massacre some dissidents. I consider the dwarven people mine already, so I won't destroy them."
